item.title: ICE Is Paying AT&T to Dig Through a Mountain of Call Records
item.author: Joseph Cox
item.content:encoded: This article was primarily reported using public records requests. We are making it available to all readers as a public service. FOIA reporting can be expensive, please consider subscribing to 404 Media to support this work. Or send us a one time donation via our tip jar here.Immigration and Customs Enforcement is paying telecommunications giant AT&T millions of dollars to have AT&T’s analysts sift through mountains of raw AT&T data for a wide variety of investigations, according to an internal ICE document obtained by 404 Media, other procurement records, and experts who reviewed those records. Civil liberty experts have called it a mass surveillance program, and they say the data can include trillions of phone records and location data. The AT&T product, interchangeably called Data Analytics and Support Services or Data Analytical Services, appears to be related to an earlier surveillance program called Hemisphere, in which AT&T provided U.S. authorities at state, local, and federal levels access to AT&T user data. Though that program shut down, ICE is still paying for access to raw data under this new arrangement with AT&T, according to the restricted ICE procurement document obtained by 404 Media. The program likely affects more than just AT&T customers because the company connects phone calls for other phone companies, meaning non-customers are likely swept up too, according to a surveillance expert.“This requirement provides ICE access to AT&T’s raw data and experienced analysts,” the document obtained by 404 Media reads.AT&T told 404 Media the data is made available under a valid legal order, but experts point out it requires an administrative subpoena, which agencies can issue themselves and don’t require a judge’s approval, raising concerns that ICE can use the data for essentially whatever it wants. The document also shows how financial incentives play a part in providing data to ICE.“The Biden administration shut down Hemisphere after I and Rep. Biggs repeatedly questioned this warrantless mass phone surveillance program. 404 Media’s reporting shows that the Trump-Vance administration has created a zombie version of Hemisphere surveillance, and given it to their chosen enforcers at ICE,” Senator Ron Wyden told 404 Media in a statement.Christopher Soghoian, a surveillance expert who worked for Senator Wyden for a decade until September, told 404 Media, “It’s bad enough that AT&T is mining its customers’ private phone records as a paid service for ICE, but because AT&T is also mining the records of other wholesale telecom companies, consumers can’t vote with their wallets and switch carriers to protect their privacy.”Last September, ICE posted a procurement record saying it awarded a contract to AT&T for access to its Data Analytics and Support Services. When ICE announced the purchase, an attached document to the listing was marked as “controlled” and not available to the public. 404 Media subsequently obtained the document through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request with ICE. The Financial Times previously reported on the public procurement records but did not report on the restricted document at the time.“OAQ [the Office of Acquisition Management] intends to procure, on a sole source basis, access to raw data and analytical services from a telecommunications company,” the restricted document reads. It says AT&T analysts will transform the AT&T data “into a suitable format” while “ensuring accurate technical interpretation to accomplish HSI’s investigative mission.” HSI is Homeland Security Investigations, the criminal investigative arm of ICE, which has traditionally focused on things like cybercrime and child abuse cases, but under the Trump administration has dramatically refocused on immigration violations and investigating voter fraud.The document says the AT&T data will be used to support “a wide range of HSI investigations and agency priorities,” but the specific sorts of investigations, taking up several lines of the document, are redacted.Another document previously obtained by Senator Wyden’s office lays out the sort of data collected by AT&T and the capabilities available under the Data Analytical Services program. Those services include linking multiple devices or phone numbers to an identified target; identifying devices that have had their SIM cards replaced; determining whether phones associated with an international investigation target have entered the U.S.; and deconflicting international phone numbers associated with targets. That document was provided by the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP), an obscure White House-affiliated entity that previously funded the Hemisphere program, and which 404 Media reported is behind a growing nationwide network of automatic license plate readers (ALPRs). According to documents previously obtained by the EFF and EPIC, the AT&T program contains more than a trillion phone records.Soghoian added AT&T also provides “wholesale service to other phone companies, helping them to deliver calls.” Through that, “AT&T is able to collect, save, and mine records of calls by customers of other companies, even conversations in which both callers use non-AT&T phone companies.”The restricted document 404 Media obtained says that during Fiscal Year 2025, there was a higher demand for data provided by this AT&T system, and “further significant increase in use is anticipated.”“AT&T is the only vendor who possesses the ability to access AT&T owned raw data,” the document continues. “The requirement is data and analytical services provided by AT&T. If AT&T does not execute the analytical work, the capability will be lost, as no other company has access to the data required.”Public procurement records show ICE paid AT&T more than $2.1 million in 2025 for access to the service, and more than $2.2 million this August, with the possibility to pay up to more than ten million dollars over the coming years.“ICE appears to have contracted for access to the same data and service AT&T provided for the Data Analytical Services (DAS) Program, formerly known as the Hemisphere Project, which is the largest telephone record collection program reported to date. ICE using DAS or something akin to it would potentially come with access to trillions of phone records and location data,” Jeramie Scott, senior counsel at EPIC and director of EPIC's Surveillance Oversight Program, told 404 Media. “This program is ripe for abuse and is being used by an agency known for the abuse of its authority.”“This is AT&T continuing to leverage its phone service to conduct mass, indiscriminate surveillance to sell to law enforcement,” Scott added. “ICE is now taking advantage of AT&T’s surveillance as a service model while likely evading any judicial oversight and conducting no privacy impact assessment prior to using the service to determine whether it should be used in the first place. Spoiler alert: It shouldn’t!”Scott pointed out the data likely includes location information too, and this raises the question whether the program violates the law given Supreme Court rulings Carpenter and Chatrie. The former ruled that law enforcement needed a warrant to obtain phone location data. The latter around location data and geofence warrants.“Americans are pushing back on government surveillance, from Flock cameras to FISA, all across the country and will be rightfully outraged that AT&T is allowing ICE to search through its customers' phone records without a warrant or court oversight,” Senator Wyden added.An AT&T spokesperson told 404 Media in an email, “For decades, we have been a trusted partner to provide reliable connectivity to federal agencies as well as state and local governments. We are required by law to provide information to government and law enforcement agencies when it is demanded under lawful order. We ensure that these requests are valid, and that our responses comply with the law.”After publication of this piece, AT&T provided a second statement: “The contract referenced is with the Department of Homeland Security to support law enforcement efforts to combat issues such as human trafficking, drug smuggling, and threats to critical infrastructure. This is not a contract supporting ICE activities, nor related to ‘surveillance’ as claimed in this inaccurate report. The program compensates AT&T for the cost of analyzing data that falls within the scope of a valid compulsory legal demand and providing the required information to law enforcement pursuant to a court order, search warrant, or subpoena. Like all carriers, AT&T is required by law to respond to valid legal demands, such as subpoenas and court orders. We ensure that these requests are valid, and that our responses comply with the law.”ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment, but previously told the Financial Times, “Nothing new here. For years law enforcement across the nation has leveraged technological innovation to fight crime. ICE is no different.”The precursor to Data Analytical Services was a program called Hemisphere. The New York Times first revealed Hemisphere in 2013, in which AT&T employees sat alongside Drug Enforcement Administration agents and supplied them with phone data going as far back as 1987. Authorities said they stopped federal funding for Hemisphere in September 2024 and shut the program down. But Data Analytical Services is essentially a continuation of that program. The document Senator Wyden’s office previously obtained says that Data Analytical Services was previously called Hemisphere.“Hemisphere is a surveillance program that refuses to die and keeps coming back with different names and different forms,” Soghoian added. “It is now clear that the Biden White House misled Congress when it said that Hemisphere had been shut down. The White House drug office funded program used by state and local law enforcement may be gone, but federal agencies are continuing to pay AT&T for the same services.”Update: this piece has been updated to include another statement from AT&T.

item.title: Yes, I want to pay for that
item.content:encoded: My last psychiatrist was terrible.Before every session, you fill out a form talking about how you’re feeling and so on as a way to evaluate whether or not your ADHD meds are working properly. For months, I’d invariably mention something about feeling pretty shitty about the political climate: ICE kidnapping people, trans folks having their very right to exist attacked, and so on.In our session, she’d ask me, without fail:But how does that affect personally?I’m a cishet white male with a strong social net. It doesn’t really affect me at all.But it affects me because I give a shit about other people, and want to see happy and successful and thriving, and holy shit what an absolutely awful question to ask someone.I see a similar conversation happen often around social services, like, “why should your taxes pay for…”Other people to go to college?Kids to eat for free at school?Free housing for a homeless person?Candy and junk food for someone on SNAP/food stamps?Someone less healthy than you to have surgery?Rehab for someone struggling with addiction?A vacation or fun experience for someone whose disabled and can’t work?Clothes for someone who can’t afford them?A toy or video game for a kid whose parents don’t work?The answer is simple: I give a shit about people.I don’t get why this is weird or confusing or controversial to anyone. I care about people, and I want to see everyone be happy and thrive.If you want to be a selfish asshole about it, we all do better when we all do better.A better educated population means a better chance of curing chronic illnesses, solving social challenges, and inventing cool new stuff.Kids who aren’t hungry learn better.People who have homes are more likely to work and less likely to use drugs or alcohol.Keeping someone alive means they can work and participate in society.Helping someone beat addiction means can work and participate in society.Keeping people clothed means they can leave the damn house, work, and participate in society.But like… I don’t give a shit if someone is “productive” or not.Everyone deserves joy and dignity and compassion, which is why I folks on SNAP or food stamps to be able to buy candy. I want poor people to experience rest and have vacations and for their kids to have toys and fun experiences.I give a shit about people.Isn’t it weird how people never ask this question about all of the awful things are taxes actually get used for right now, today? As a US citizen, my taxes are used to…Kidnap minorities and ship them to illegal labor prisons.Clutter space with internet satellites that fuck up astronomy.Poison the water, soil, and air with industrial waste.Rapidly accelerate planetary warming.I’d much rather some poor kid gets a hot meal or someone who will never work gets to eat a fucking Snickers bar than any of those things.Because I give a shit about people.If you’re upset at the idea that your tax money might prevent someone from dying but upset that your taxes are used to literally murder people, you’re the weirdo, not me.

item.title: The Failed Promise Of Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson Fund
item.author: Vince Grzegorek
item.content:encoded: After the Cleveland Browns traded for Deshaun Watson in March 2022, team owners Jimmy and Dee Haslam hopped on Zoom for an awkward press conference. They couldn’t simply cop to willfully ignoring the numerous credible allegations that Watson had sexually assaulted or harassed massage therapists. The Haslams ran a disastrous organization long in need of a franchise quarterback, and they had just acquired him for three first-round picks, two fourth-round picks, and a third-round pick, in what many have called the worst trade in NFL history. It sounds pretty disgusting when you put it like that, so the owners equivocated and attempted to justify it."I think it is important for you to understand how seriously we took this whole process," Jimmy Haslam said. "Dee and I both have close friends who have been victims—men and women—of sexual abuse. We have seen up close the impact it has had on their lives, both short and long term. It is something we take very, very seriously. [...] I know we can both say, as can others in our organization, that we put more time, more thought, more effort, talked to more people and did more research on this decision by far than any other decision we have made with the Cleveland Browns. It is not something we took lightly. It is something we took very seriously, and we feel comfortable with the process we have been through."The two co-owners would use the word "comfortable" more than a dozen times during the press conference, which is notably a very different word than "confident" or "ecstatic." The Haslams were comfortable with the process, with Watson as a person, with trading that pile of draft picks to Houston, and with handing Watson a $230 million contract that was guaranteed at signing. They were also comfortable with the legal system’s ability to handle the matter.

item.title: Trying to Avoid a Cold
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Cold and flu season are ramping up, so let's take two minutes to consider something you've never really thought about before. Where is the place you are most likely to run into someone who has a communicable illness? In bed, sure, but you can avoid other people's beds. You might say the doctor's office, but if you're willing to spend your time and money there, that means you're already pretty sick (at least in America). No, it's the store aisle where the cold remedies are. When there's a bug going around, that aisle is liable to be crowded with suspicious shoppers. You could order symptom relief through Door Dash, but those gig workers are desperate enough to work while sick, and will sneeze on your package.

item.title: Charting American Culture in News Footage of ‘Grand Theft Auto’
item.author: Matthew Gault
item.content:encoded: Some people spent the week leading up to the release of replaying the old games. I, sicko that I am, spent it watching TV news coverage of the franchise from the past 20 years.Grand Theft Auto has been a staple of cable and broadcast TV news since at least the release of in 2001. I’ve been an adult for all of it; I’ve had a front row seat for two decades of moral panics, parental freakouts, and bizarre political theater. The games and the broader culture’s reaction to them have changed dramatically in that time. In 2001, newscasters worried GTA III was training an army of young men to kill. In 2026, earnestly quoted Bell Hooks in its review of GTA VI.For mainstream news, GTA is the ur-video game. The open world that mirrors our own, the prevalence of sex and death, and the increasingly realistic simulations and graphics pointed towards the dream of what a video game could be. GTA is the American id made manifest.You can chart America’s changing culture — especially its anxieties — by watching how the media covered Grand Theft Auto. This was, at first, the game that critics of the medium had always warned us about: a violent sex and death simulator that rotted the brains of the youth just as rock and roll and comics had done in ages past. Twenty years on, the brains are thoroughly rotted, GTA won, and now? Now we’re all worried about money.GTA III and — Murder Simulators, the Assassin of YouthRockstar released in October 2001 and just a year later. The controversy around both started right away and centered around violence, and sometimes, the game’s depiction of women. “This is the world’s most popular video game [...] and millions of kids are mastering it by learning to slaughter bystanders,” Ted Koppel told America.Nightline devoted 20 minutes of its broadcast to GTA in July 2002. It interviewed children who grinned ear to ear as they gunned down people in GTA, their parents who insisted it was just a game, a concerned expert who was sure GTA was training them to kill, and a psychologist who said that was bullshit. It all ended with a roundtable discussion where a police officer, in uniform, explained the differences between video games and real world violence.Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — Congressional Hearings and Sex on TVI was an assistant manager of a Gamestop in Texas in 2004 when Rockstar released Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The level of parental concern in the store was high in the weeks leading up to its release. One mother was so upset by a bearing a cover story about that she told me I was going to hell for “selling a gangster lifestyle” to children.But it was sex, not violence, that the news focused on with . The game had a lot of simulation elements — its protagonist would gain weight if he ate too much — and Rockstar had experimented with a sex minigame called “hot coffee.” Developers cut the minigame from the final release, but it was still on the physical discs that went to stores. Modders uncovered it in the files and were able to patch it back in.California politician Leland Yee got wind of the mod and condemned the Entertainment Software Ratings Board (ESRB) for labeling the game “Mature” instead of “Adults Only.” Cable news went wild. Rachel Maddow weighed in. Hillary Clinton, then a Senator in New York, demanded an investigation. Congress voted to send the FTC after Rockstar for deceiving the ESRB. The ESRB updated the game’s rating to an AO. Walmart, Best Buy, and other retailers . publisher Take-Two shipped new copies with the content completely removed. Take-Two’s shareholders also removed most of its board and put Strauss Zelnick in charge. He’s been the CEO ever since.— The Ballad of Jack ThompsonThe cultural winds had shifted by the time hit stores in 2008. Retailers across the country had midnight release parties where people lined up to purchase the game as soon as possible. Local news outlets interviewed people in line and marveled at how much money might make.But the culture warriors still pointed to GTA as proof of America’s moral decline. Glenn Beck, then an anchor on CNN Headline News, on the game and often spoke to American lawyer Jack Thompson. Thompson hated Grand Theft Auto so much and was so sure it was training young people to kill their elders that he let his crusade against the franchise ruin his life.Thompson against Take-Two aimed at preventing the company from selling at all. The publisher counter-sued, Thompson accused it of perjury, and the parties eventually settled. In its ruling, the courts said Thompson could never use the legal system to stop Take-Two from publishing a game ever again.He didn’t stop though. After the game came out, Thompson Rockstar had based an assassination mission on him. He then sent a letter to Strauss Zelnick’s mom. “Your son, this very moment, is doing everything he possibly can to sell as many copies of GTA IV to teen boys in the United States, a country in which your son claims you raised him to be ‘a Boy Scout.’ More like the Hitler Youth, I would say. Happy Mother’s day, Mrs. Zelnick, which this year is May 11, two weeks after your son unleashes porn and violence upon other mothers’ boys. I'm sure you’re very proud,” Thompson wrote in the letter.The Supreme Court of Florida permanently disbarred him shortly thereafter.Money in the Age of ViolenceIn 2013, made a billion dollars in three days and was the biggest entertainment release of all time. It made more money than any movie, book, album, or video game had ever made before. Every news broadcast about the game led with that fact. “Never has there been an opening like this in the entertainment industry,” CBS News said.Jake Tapper and CNET’s Dan Ackerman lamented that GTA V’s success would hurt the creativity of the video game industry. “It’s become such a hit-driven business. You have to have a big opening day or opening weekend for anyone to take you seriously. And when you have such a hit-driven business, I think people get risk averse and they don’t get as creative,” Ackerman told Tapper. The news still ran segments about the violence and sex in the game, but it was typically couched in a conversation about its runaway financial success. Most anchors brought on experts who told them about the business. They sought to understand what was happening and why people liked the game, rather than condemning it outright. Anxieties of American DeclineIn 2026, cultural fears about violence and sex in video games are gone. Instead, we’re all worried about money. Everyone is sure will make money, the question is if it will make the money?“Why the stakes for GTA VI are so high,” declared the thumbnail for a Bloomberg video about the game. The outlet’s podcast also ran an episode about why the . Newsweek worried that the U.S. economy as people take time off work to play. CBS News’ morning show wondered how much money the game would make and the anchor admitted he once “lost a summer” to Grand Theft Auto. No one discussed violence at all. CNBC’s coverage called the game a “Billion Dollar Hype Machine.”Behind it all is a kind of lament — a worry that might be a final hurrah for this kind of game. Rumors are that it cost a billion dollars. Games are more expensive than ever and the industry has been devastated. A third of the industry lost their jobs in the past 24 months and most of them . Even when a game is successful, companies cut staff. wondered if GTA VI “may be the last great heist.”Underneath all these economic fears, the older panics still lurked. On Fox News, middling collegiate swimmer turned political activist Riley Gaines hoped that the game’s romantic elements would lead to a rise in birth rates. “Hopefully these men realize they like the feeling of love, romantic love, and go out and find it. Because, I’ll tell you what, we’re in a population decline. We need more babies. You can’t have babies, real babies, mouths to feed, from video games,” Gaines said.Twitch streamer Sasha Grey had early access to the game and was streaming it to YouTube and Twitch when YouTube shut down her stream for “nudity.” An early cutscene showed what Grey described as “artistic nip and some booty.” Grey complained to YouTube in a post on X and shared a screenshot of the moment the company shut down her stream. “They allow far worse under their educational category. This game is art, y’know? It’s the biggest release of the friggin’ decade,” Grey said during her stream. She pulled up the post on X to see if she’d gotten a response. “Oh god, the Twitter post got labeled as adult content, which means it’s going to be harder to get seen.”The old protestant advertiser-friendly anti-sex morality is still there, programmed into the computer systems we use every day.

item.title: ICE List Confirms the Identities of 5,000 Immigration Agents
item.author: Andre Costa
item.content:encoded: ICE List has confirmed the identities of more than 5,000 immigration agents, more than double the roughly 2,200 on our public record on 28 October, the day a staff directory of the Department of Homeland Security was leaked.The leak, is available to the public via the transparency group DDoSecrets under the name Icepick, holds 41,191 records of DHS employees and contractors. A group calling itself the Department of Peace says it took them through the single sign-on service DHS buys from Okta. Okta says it has "no evidence our data or systems were compromised". DHS said it was "aware of a potential breach".A name in the leak does not get anyone onto ICE List. The leak tells us where to look, and a page goes up only when we can tie the name to an agent through a source outside it, such as a court filing, an official record or press reporting. About 2,270 of the named agents on the record are documented in court filings, most of them filed by the government itself.Crucially, a number of the people named in the leak no longer work at ICE, and some have retired. The directory covers the whole department, with 21,329 records from Customs and Border Protection and 6,598 from ICE, and it is a list of accounts, which is a different thing from a list of the people making arrests today. Those who have moved on from the agency show the crucial need for a steady hand with information like this. The ICE List is targeted at the Trump regime's transformation of ICE and Border Patrol, and many of those who left as soon as Trump took charge may indeed oppose the tactics that are now commonplace. For now we are working only through the field agents. We will go through the remaining names afterwards to see whether any have joined ICE or CBP since.More than 20 of the names we have confirmed were searched for on our site from DHS and ICE work computers. Our logs record the network a search comes from and cannot show who typed it. They do show that somebody inside the department went looking for those names on ICE List before we had published them. DHS's own network sent more than 10,000 requests to the site in the two weeks to 29 October.We do not publish home addresses, phone numbers or email addresses. This is a common claim by opponents of our project, and indeed, by the US government itself. As confirmed by multiple investigations, no addresses appear on the ICE List. ICE agents make arrests in masks, in plain clothes and from unmarked cars, and the Trump regime refuses to name them even after they have shot someone. DHS says naming agents puts them and their families in danger. The agents on this record are public officials using the powers of the state in public, and in most cases the government has already named them in a courtroom.Every page lists its sources. Anyone who believes they have been named in error can contact us and we will check the record against the evidence. Footage, documents and names can be sent to the same place.ICE Watch, the app the public uses to send footage, photos and plate numbers to ICE List, is now in testing on Google Play. Join the test to install it on your phone.ICE List and Crust News are paid for by readers. Subscribe to get our reporting by email, or donate to keep the record growing.

item.title: Trifect Up Beyond Repair
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: My first thought upon watching the Trump/Xi/Putin dictators-in-triplicate fest was that it’s too bad the air travel ground stop didn’t last another week. Trump’s international trips are like an endless Matryoshka doll, with each subsequent international humiliation being worse than the last. And this one was that, times three. The axis of evil has been replaced by the dictatorial triple threat, and the American president is an enthusiastic member of the troika. The whole style over substance affair could, I suppose, be viewed as a win, win, win. Xi got to look like the host with the most leader of the world. Putin, a murderous mafia boss of a semi-failed state, got images that make him look like he’s on equal footing with the world’s superpowers. And Trump got to fawn over his frenemies, in addition to bringing his traveling one-man slumber party to an international audience. I don’t blame him for being tired. Betrayal is more exhausting than it looks. Never judge a man until you’ve walked a mile on his bone spurs. Sadly, with all that winning, no one was at the summit to represent American interests. The land of the free was replaced by the land of the three. Oh well, you win some you threesome. I’d like to be more positive, but you can’t polish a third.+ Here’s the excellent Anne Applebaum with a look at some of the trilateral collateral. “Its true purpose was not to end any wars—and certainly not to end Russia’s bloody invasion of Ukraine—but to produce propaganda photographs and video clips that each of the three leaders will now use to mask their political failures. Certainly this was President Trump’s main goal. Before the three leaders met, he actually told Fox News that the most significant moment was already over: ‘the greeting yesterday, which in the history of China has never happened.’ Xi Jinping, aware of how easy it is to manipulate the American president, had met Trump at his airplane, on the tarmac … For Vladimir Putin, the meeting also created useful propaganda. Now almost five years into a war he believed he would win in three days, he is coping with 1.5 million war casualties; the loss, as of this week, of half of his country’s oil-refining capacity; and even, in the past few days, the destruction of the Kerch Strait Bridge, which links Russia to Crimea … Nevertheless, Putin will use the Shenzhen meeting to tell Russians that their country is still a superpower, still allowed to sit in the same room as the Americans and the Chinese … For Xi, the meeting was useful because he was the host, he set up the photographs, and his propaganda was broadcast around the world. With Trump’s cooperation, he telegraphed American decline, Chinese power, and Russian subservience.” Trump’s Embarrassing, Inconsequential Summit.+ “Mr. Trump, who has spoken for years with admiration about both autocrats, gushed about being welcomed by the two men. ‘We are really making history,’ he said at their meeting.” (Nothing has gone down in history quite as fast as America’s international leadership role under Trump.) (Gift Article): Behind Trump Meeting, Xi and Putin Share a Vision of Usurping U.S. Power.+ It really was all worse than I’m making it sound. Especially the sick love Trump showed for Putin, his “friend” with whom he has a “great relationship.” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk responded with this: “God, protect us from such friends.”One of the more anticipated IPOs in years has finally taken place as Anthropic hit the public markets. The stock initially soared well above its offering price, but then Claude thawed, and it has since settled into more traditional, solid first-day performance. The rest of the market suffered another rough day. Here’s the latest: Anthropic Shares Climb After Multibillion-Dollar I.P.O. “Anthropic has become by far the most valuable company on the stock market with the legal designation of a public benefit corporation, or P.B.C. That status requires Anthropic to prioritize its corporate mission — to develop safe artificial intelligence systems ‘for the long-term benefit of humanity.'” (If, you know, humanity survives the long term.)At the risk of bringing back memories of the great toilet paper rush of 2020, I should let you know that the tech outages of the past week have driven some panic buying at Costco and Walmart. Generators are a big hit, as is general pantry loading. (But if the internet goes down, is there still a point in living?) The prepper crowd is way ahead of the rest of us. But the rest of us are starting to join the prepper crowd. “Once written off as paranoid fantasy, and largely the domain of those with conservative and libertarian views, prepping itself has rapidly joined the mainstream and, in some quarters, has taken on a liberal bent: Rather than hiding away alone, armed to the teeth, there is an emphasis on building resilience and connections among people.” (Gift Article): They’re Prepping for a Broken Digital World. “DoorDash is not an emergency plan.” (Of course not. You need to back it up with UberEats and GrubHub.)+ “We believe many of the major disruptions of the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams simply cannot patch these vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising their production environments. The second effect is the rise of AI-assisted cyberattacks. Bad actors are using open-weight models and new agentic frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed and scale.” Palo Alto Networks CEO just dropped a truth bomb on the network outages.+ As I explained yesterday, while it looks like our computers weren’t hacked, the events of the last week made it plainly clear that have been.While some of us are stocking up on toilet paper, others still don’t have access to toilets. And it just happens to be World Toilet Day, a funny idea with a serious goal. “The U.N. has stated that access to safe sanitation is a human right. And in just about every country, progress has been made in improving access to sanitary facilities. Since 2015, 1.2 billion people have become part of the world of safely managed sanitation systems.” And from Chris Mims in the (Gift Article): I Tried New York City’s New High-Tech Public Bathrooms—and Saw the Future. “On a day-long tour of New York City’s new, high-tech public bathrooms this week, I found them remarkably tidy—as did the many New Yorkers whom I cornered both before and after they used them.” (Being immediately confronted by a reporter after using a public restroom sounds like something out of an IBS nightmare.)Iowa Chu Talking About, Willis? “The U.S. Army’s plan to detonate about 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals that have become unstable and might explode if moved has some Iowa residents worried that a cloud of lead dust could cause environmental contamination and health problems. The detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is set for Friday, and officials recommend that some residents in nearby Middletown vacate the area. If they can’t leave their homes, they should stay inside and keep windows and doors closed.” (Even though they also warn that the blast could break some windows.) Iowans brace for a lead dust cloud as Army plans to detonate 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals.+ Turn Your Head and Witkoff: “SEC filings reveal that the president’s son-in-law is negotiating for peace while profiting from war.” Jared Kushner’s Undisclosed Investment. (In fairness, I don’t think Jared has an official government role.)+ What the Heil is He Talking About? (Robot voice) Attention plebeians and other human life forms, I am not MAGA and was never really MAGA. Please save this data to your hard drive. Elon Musk claims ‘I’m not MAGA‘ and says he regrets vast sums to back Republicans. (Well, I believe the second part…)+ After a year during which her megahit Choosin’ Texas dominated the charts, “Ella Langley set a new, all-time record for the most CMA Awards wins in one night on Wednesday.” But my favorite milestone of the night was achieved by NextDraft-approved artist Stephen Wilson Jr, who won best new artist at the age of 47. Here’s his CMA performance with Chris Stapleton. A decade ago, he was a scientist shepherding the creation of a digestible dental-cleaning chew for dogs. Years after leaving that gig for a full-time music career, he burst onto the scene in 2024 with this viral cover of Stand by Me.

item.title: Time Wharp
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to Time Wharp, an American multi-instrumentalist from Atlanta. The project is by Kaye Loggins, now based in Brooklyn. She played in bands in high school – punk, ska, metal, and “Myspace comedy techno” as she told Into. Terry Riley and the compilation pointed her towards ambient and experimental music. Her solo work as Time Wharp reflects her individual vision and unique collection of happenstance influences. Her album was released in 2022 on Leaving Records, manifesting the label’s “all-genre” ethos. There are elements of minimalism, jazz, leftfield electronic… First, though, we’re playing Radical American Hippy Kraut, whose “Blues 4 dANA” ended our neo-krautrock mix this week. It’s a collaboration with New York’s Charley Lanning aka CH Rom.

item.title: There’s A New Disruptor Throwing Terrible AI Slop At Sports Fans
item.author: Chris Thompson
item.content:encoded: The new Beatline Sports network features daily blog posts and podcast episodes for every team across eight professional sports leagues, plus men's college basketball and college football. Well, "features" might be the wrong verb. Let's try again: The new Beatline Sports network shits a torrent of flagrantly worthless content into the digital media ecosystem, at a cadence of more than 300 podcast episodes per day, plus blog posts. All of this is created using what we have resigned ourselves to referring to as generative artificial intelligence.Judging by its catalog of episodes, Beatline's podcast operation went live sometime around Aug. 20; every day since, it has dumped out one short episode per team, per league. Beatline gained widespread internet attention this week when sports reporter and podcaster Sarah Spain made fun of its phony NWSL coverage. A little while later, accounts purportedly belonging to Ibnul Jaif Farabi, identified as Beatline's founder on the website, began replying to critics, deploying the sneering tone of the tech disruptor. I'm using hedged language here because social media identification verification is a joke, and we are far enough through the looking glass that the account itself could be a cheap AI construct. If it's Farabi, he is a huge asshole. If it's not him, whoever's doing it is also a huge asshole."I'm the guy behind the Beatline Sports," Farabi's account wrote on Twitter. "If one person doing this 300+ sports podcasts daily, with custom created models and agents on CPU only, then you need to question your profession my guy. Compete or perish. The whole thing costs me like 5 cents daily though, altogether." Farabi seems to be growing comfortable with villainy, although he describes himself as "kind" and "warm-hearted" in a self-profile on About.Me, with the natural exception of "those days when for no apparent reason I hate pretty much everyone."

item.title: What Happens to Your Body When You Die?
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Kurzgesagt explores what happens to your body when you die.Death isn’t a single switch that shuts down your entire body at once. When your heart stops beating and your brain goes silent, trillions of cells inside you are still alive, desperately trying to keep themselves running. Death isn’t a single moment, but a slow and surprisingly complex process that can last for weeks.What actually happens when you die? What makes death so mysterious, and which cells are the last survivors within your body?

item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: Adaptation is a tricky process. Representing source material created in one medium within the formal and aesthetic environment of another, without changing the original material in the process, is impossible. As is the case with any sort of translation, the adapter must digest and synthesize the source material, then find some way to reproduce its poetic truths while accommodating as much of its structural skeleton as they care to or are capable of. The concept of a "faithful adaptation" supposes a perfectly reflective surface that does not exist.That said, Netflix's adaptation of Cixin Liu's brilliant novel is a disaster. I hated it. Not necessarily because it changed key parts of the foundational Remembrance of Earth's Past sci-fi trilogy, though it did, but more because it failed to represent any of the thematic or conceptual gnarliness that made the books so good. The show's first season, overseen by duo David Benioff and D. B. Weiss and stylized as for some reason, debuted in March 2024, and the second season drops this coming January, as revealed in a trailer earlier this week. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IrpS1G5tB7w

item.title: Rich People Collecting Unicorn Horns
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Once you have enough money to buy all the fine objects and comforts available to you, the rich are left with a desire to be admired by others. The easy way to do that is to buy more stuff, as long as those objects are rare, expensive, and liable to draw attention. In the 16th and 17th centuries, there was a world of these curious objects available from world explorers and traders. Wealthy people collected exotic art from faraway places and natural specimens never seen before, or even better both in one object, into curiosity cabinets. Explaining these impressive objects raised one's status in a way mere money didn't, even when that explanation was nonsense. Evan Puschak explores the rise of curiosity cabinets and the forces that made them a thing. (via kottke)

item.title: Bringing the Largest Public ICE Database to Your Phone
item.author: Dominick Skinner
item.content:encoded: After months of rejections, the ICE Watch app has been accepted onto the Google Play store, and we can now invite testers to join and help get the app approved for a full release. Many people will not want to install the app through the store, and the .apk install is still available at its old location. The Play Store will not replace the third party routes.We will pursue an iPhone version as soon as the app passes through the testing period on Android.ICE Watch is the app that lets the public contribute to The ICE List. It has had limited use so far because we could not get it approved for the official Android app store.On November 13, a US federal judge issued a permanent injunction barring the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security from pressuring Apple and Meta to suppress platforms used to monitor ICE activity. That injunction is the reason we chose now to resubmit the app to the Play Store, and may be the reason it was accepted.Google puts a new app through a closed test before it can go onto the store for everyone. A set of testers has to install it and keep it for two weeks before anyone else can. We need those testers now.The app has been in use for five months, so this is early access more than a test.With the app you can swipe through documented ICE operations and the agents nobody has named yet, Tinder-style, and help identify the agents we have not been able to.The full ICE List is in the app too. Browse by state, and send footage or a tip from your phone in seconds. Share a video from your gallery straight to us. Nothing you send appears publicly until a person has reviewed it, and tips are anonymous.We made one serious change for the Google Play version: logins are gone. Anyone who installs from the Play Store gets an anonymous ID. This makes no real difference to most users, but the groups who work alongside us have been asked to install from the F-Droid store or the .apk file instead.If you want to help test it, leave the email of a Google account on your phone at blog.theicelist.org/testers. We will send you a link to install the app. Keep it for three weeks, use it as you would anyway, and tell us what, if anything, breaks at icelist@crustnews.com.If you use an iPhone, you do not have to wait for the iOS app. Open watch.theicelist.org in Safari, tap the Share button at the bottom of the screen, then tap Add to Home Screen. ICE Watch then opens from your home screen like any other app, full screen, and you can send footage and tips from it the same way.The ICE List takes no advertising and no institutional money. It is funded by the public. If you want to help this project grow, please consider supporting it here.

item.title: Godzilla Minus Any Reason For This Sequel To Exist
item.author: Kathryn Xu
item.content:encoded: A couple of weeks ago, my friend's sister texted him, insisting that he must go see the new Godzilla movie, , which is, naturally, the sequel to . She wanted him to see it so badly that she Venmo'd him, sponsoring the movie tickets, and was checking in every day to ask if he'd seen it yet. So when our local climbing gym workers went on strike on Tuesday morning, trying to negotiate their first contract since unionizing in 2023, we nixed our original plans for the evening and bumped up the viewing date instead. My friend informed his sister that we had bought tickets; ok now that u have tickets, she responded, .The bribe was not because the movie was so good that we simply had to see it, but because she knew that it would be disappointing to pay to go see a bad movie, so she was reimbursing him in advance. It was one of the most masterful cons I have experienced in my adult life, and one abetted by the fact that we watched , a legitimately good monster movie, in anticipation. is set in the immediate aftermath of World War II, returning Godzilla back to its 1954 roots as a metaphor for the hydrogen bomb. All of 's characters are still wrestling with trauma from the war, especially the main character, Kōichi Shikishima, who was a failed kamikaze pilot. The ending message is a hopeful and humanist one: that war is terrible, that every human life is precious and worthwhile, that the most important thing is to live. Mostly, the movie expresses this by putting Shikishima through the absolute wringer.

item.author: Sabrina Imbler
item.content:encoded: In his 22nd career NHL game, Winnipeg Jets rookie Viggo Bjorck finally broke through with his first career goal. Drafted eighth overall out of Sweden, the 18-year-old has been a fixture in the Winnipeg lineup since opening night, but he'd turned in nothing of note during a start that also included a nine-game team losing streak. However, as the Jets have found a winning groove in the last few weeks, Bjorck has picked up a few assists, and even though they didn't beat the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday, he earned this major milestone in the game's second period.Bjorck blew people away with his offensive prowess as a teen playing against other teens, though his relatively slight size (5-foot-9, 177 pounds) is something to overcome. Ideally, he plays center for the Jets, but lately they've switched him over to wing, which could simplify the game for a slumping youngster.

item.title: datasette-arrows 0.1a0
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Datasette 1.0a43 added the ability for plugins to implement streaming export formats. Datasette core supports streaming CSV and TSV - you can export millions of lines of data from a table without needing to load it all into memory, because those two file formats support streaming data in chunks. The register_output_renderer() plugin hook can now be used to implement the same pattern for other formats.I've learned never to release a new plugin feature without accompanying it with a plugin that uses it.Claude Fable 5.2 suggested the Apache Arrow streaming format as a good option, and built this plugin in almost a single shot.Add the plugin to Datasette (datasette install datasette-arrows) and the export dialog gains this new Arrow option:This screenshot is from Datasette's branch - the most recent release doesn't yet group streaming formats such as Arrow with the TSV and CSV in the "All rows in this table" section, but that's coming in the next alpha release.

item.title: A Peek at What We Still Don’t Know About the Worst of Trump II … So Far
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Trump Sicced the IRS on ProtestersI hinted in yesterday’s Unsanctioned that one of the major benefits of Congress reviving its oversight powers under new Democratic majorities will be to provide a fuller accounting of what’s already happened in the first two years of Trump II.As bad as it’s been on the retribution, corruption, and destruction fronts, we only know a fraction of what’s really gone down. Vigorous congressional oversight — absent under the GOP majorities — promises to gives us a clearer picture of the worst of the Trump II depredations, like the mass deportation operation, and uncover wrongdoing we don’t even know about yet.We get a new peek today at what that might look like in a NYT story that shows the IRS directly involved in targeting left-wing political groups in the aftermath of the assassination of Charlie Kirk. The IRS “initiated at least four criminal investigations” into as-yet-unidentified left-wing groups, according to a portion of an internal memo obtained by the NYT.“The memo describes the work done by a group of a dozen I.R.S. officials detailed to a task force formed in response to Mr. Kirk’s death on Sept. 10, 2025,” the NYT reports.As TPM’s Josh Kovensky has reported at length, while the Trump administration ostentatiously turned Kirk’s death into a national day of mourning, it also seized on the assassination as a pretext to criminalize dissent, invent a left-wing terrorism threat that it falsely claimed had international connections, and scrutinize left-wing political and advocacy groups in an effort to intimidate and cow protests.In the two weeks after Kirk’s death, President Trump designated Antifa as a terrorist organization and signed National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (NSPM-7). In NSPM-7, Trump ordered the IRS commissioner “to ensure that no tax-exempt entities are directly or indirectly financing political violence or domestic terrorism” and to refer such organizations and their officers and employees to the DOJ for investigation and prosecution.“The memo viewed by The Times is the first window into the work the I.R.S. has actually undertaken to carry out the demands from the White House,” according to the story.In March of this year, the IRS criminal investigations branch began working with the the task force that was operating out of the FBI headquarters, according to the NYT story. The memo covers work done between March and July. The NYT said it reviewed the first six pages of the eight-page memo. The last two pages, which the newspaper did not see, apparently identified the four targeted groups.The protests at Delany Hall, the immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey, have been a particular focus of the task force:I.R.S. officials reviewed financial information, including subpoenaed Venmo records, about people arrested during those protests, as well as businesses that the officials believed could be funding them. At one point, I.R.S. officials used facial recognition and tattoo analysis databases to help identify individuals, the memo said.A quick summary of some of the memo’s highlights, as reported by the NYT:In addition to the Delaney Hall protests, the IRS also assisted in the response to the April shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, the May shooting at a mosque in San Diego, and the June UFC event on the White House lawn. It’s not clear from the memo what role the IRS had in the UFC event (five men were charged with allegedly plotting to attack the event).At least four tax-exempt groups were referred to the civil side of the agency, which conducts audits;IRS officials have been assigned to nine grand juries.The memo is just a glimpse into one discrete operation during one window of time this year, and it alone can’t really provide a clear picture of the scale and scope of the effort to turn political opposition to the Trump administration into criminal conduct. That’s one area where a Democratic Congress could bring new facts to light and begin to back the Trump administration off from its worst excesses.President Trump brought an ignominious end to the political career of Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) by endorsing the scoundrel Ken Paxton and costing Texas a Senate seat — and now it’s having knock-on effects in the final weeks before Cornyn leaves office.Cornyn appears to be very much on board with having Ohio native T. Elliot Gaiser — the head of the Trump DOJ’s Office of Legal Counsel — installed as a federal judge in Texas, where he has few personal or professional connections.A coveted federal judgeship going to a non-Texan while bypassing the home state senators’ approved list of potential nominees would be a tough ask by any president under any circumstance (unless you’re Ted Cruz, I guess). But under these circumstances, it’s a lot to expect Cornyn to roll over after getting royally screwed:Cornyn’s remarks came as Bloomberg reported that last year, early in his tenure at OLC, Gaiser pitched a memo that proposed reviving the 1873 Comstock Act to criminalize the transportation of abortion drugs and related medical supplies.Then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche rejected Gaiser’s pitch, according to Bloomberg’s sources: “Blanche pushed back by directing him to table the issue due to his worry that Gaiser’s position would amount to a federal abortion ban — an issue the administration had avoided wading into before the midterms …”In an unusual move, Gaiser contacted Bloomberg directly after it published its story and denied it. “Your story is categorically false, period,” Gaiser said. “I did not push for any nationwide abortion ban.”Where Have You Found AI Most Useful?I ask this question with some trepidation. For a number of reasons, I have been slow to take affirmative steps to incorporate AI into my personal and professional lives.I haven’t activated AI on my Apple devices or integrated it into Google yet. I’ve played around with Claude for maybe two hours over the past six months, and I used Gemini to create a couple of satirical images to make a friend laugh (with mixed results). I’ve not touched ChatGPT, and I haven’t used any of the new personal AI agents like Muse.But I am curious about AI’s utility and how you’re incorporating it as a tool in your lives and work. I’m also pretty leery of the privacy risks involved — so I’d be interested in hearing where you’re drawing the line on entrusting AI tools with personal or sensitive information.At this point, I should acknowledge that AI is a dreadfully imprecise term so let me refine what I mean for the purposes of this question. If you’re scientist, engineer, developer, or otherwise use AI at a high technical level, I’m probably not looking for for feedback from you. But even that can be a fuzzy line to draw. For example, a friend who is not a professional coder used AI to code a draftboard for his fantasy baseball team. So the newest AI tools may put some of what we used to think of as technical work within reach of a layperson. Obviously the AI I’m talking about here is a far cry from the frontier work on artificial general intelligence. You get the idea.Let me try to preempt the emails warning me about the evils of AI or how you’re not using it and will never use it. I get you. My own slow adoption of AI is partly because it gives me pause, too. This has been a new frontier of consumer tech that I’ve been content not to be on the cutting edge of. But it’s pervasiveness at what I’ll call the retail level — quite apart from its role in research and development, core science, and other technical applications — has me prepared to adapt … possibly.Thanks in advance for your feedback. My contact information is immediately below.

item.title: What Referees Really Think About Automated Officiating Coming To The NBA
item.author: Ben Dowsett
item.content:encoded: Video replay once held so much promise in team sports. We would never have to watch another perfect game get ruined, never have to experience the agony of a blown call ending our team’s season.Instead we’ve mostly gotten tedious, largely illogical uses of replay. Goals are routinely called back in the NHL because a few inches of an attacking player’s skate crossed the blue line in an offside position, even if it happened a full minute before the puck went in the net; the use of VAR in the Premier League has been so disastrous that the phrase “Well done, boys, good process” resurfaces as a grim joke every time the replay officials make a mess of something; replay has somehow made the definition of a catch in football to agree on.

item.title: Broken World
item.author: Jason Koebler
item.content:encoded: Very chonky newsletter today as we have published quite a lot over the last 24 hours. Today we look into why everything is busted and have an extremely wild story about how people are using their AI agents. A few hours ago, I went to rent a Lime bike to ride the ten minutes to my therapy appointment. I opened Lime, scanned the QR code, and double clicked my iPhone’s side button to authorize Apple Pay. The app hung for a few moments, then closed. I tried several more times and the same thing happened. In the back of my mind, I wondered what was going on — was the Lime bike broken? Was my cell phone service out? Was it something else? I opened the Uber app and, similarly, wasn’t able to pay. I opened DownDetector and realized that the entirety of Apple Pay, a thing I thought existed only on my phone and not the cloud, was down. I texted my therapist, put my phone in my pocket, and started jogging. Not being able to rent a Lime Bike for several minutes is an extremely minor inconvenience barely worth mentioning. And yet the mental gymnastics my brain did in those few minutes — what’s broken, why is it broken, how is it broken — is something that everyone I know have been repeatedly doing for the last few weeks as seemingly every service and system crashes down around us. Over the weekend, people who I do not normally talk to about my job asked me: What is going on with the airplanes? Why is my bank down? What about Microsoft? The default assumption that many people are making is that these are either being caused by cyberattacks and/or “AI” broadly defined, whether that’s AI gone haywire, “rogue” AI agents, or something else, which is indicative of just how fearful people are of AI. What I have been telling people is, basically, that shit is broken and things are going to keep breaking. For lots of different reasons. It’s often not a hack and it’s often not explicitly AI-related, but everything now sort of looks like that XKCD comic of the dependency domino tower. While not exactly true that AI and cyberattacks are causing these outages, it’s also not entirely wrong, either. What we’re seeing is — I think — a series of infrastructure failures (and some cyberattacks) that are not directly connected but are broadly a symptom of the same general trends and systemic problems we’ve seen across society, the government, and the tech sector over the last several years. First, it’s worth mentioning that anytime there’s a string of outages, there’s a tendency to tie them altogether. And outages or hacks that previously wouldn’t have been noted at all suddenly get more attention and become part of the narrative. Take, for example, the fact that the International Ice Hockey Federation has been targeted by a cyberattack; you probably would not normally hear about this but it has suddenly become part of the broader story. The simplest explanation I can come up with for the broader disastrous trend we’ve seen is that since the pandemic we have seen: mass layoffs of tech workers and software developers mass deployment of AI-assisted and vibe coded products, software updates, and patchesmass layoffs in the government sector and outright destruction of government expertise and oversightthe loss of institutional knowledge associated with those layoffs and funding cutsa failure to invest in upgrading infrastructure/redundancygovernment contracts handed out to the President’s friends and political alliesAI and LLM-assisted/iterative exploit discovery, coding, and deploymentcompanies responding to the AI hacking threat with AI-coded and rushed patchesWhen Elon Musk took over Twitter and named it X, there were many people who thought his layoffs and the associated loss of expertise would result in the site failing basically because of an infrastructural failure. Twitter would basically “go down” because someone would break something and no one would know how to fix it. We haven’t really seen that happen to X, but that same philosophy of firing the experts and YOLOing AI into everything while hoping shit doesn’t break is now the explicit strategy of our entire economy and our entire government. This segment is a paid ad. If you’re interested in advertising, Use code 404MEDIA A man and his Muse sue MetaA little over a week ago, Meta suspended the Facebook pages belonging to Joe Thomas, the owner of South Carolina-based Kong Koatings Epoxy Countertops. For the last few months, Thomas’ Muse agent Baby Mia (which is named after his granddaughter) has run different parts of his business, which includes making and posting AI-generated videos on several of his company’s Facebook pages. The videos feature, for example, AI versions of Thomas and his wife pouring epoxy on a floor and their feet. After Thomas gave the AI agent access to his Facebook pages, Meta’s content moderation disabled the accounts because it suspected that the agent itself was a hacker. Because Thomas does all of his business’s marketing through Facebook ads, he says his inbound leads stopped while his accounts were disabled.“I use AI for everything I do. All my emails, she runs my business. I’ve used it so much, Mia is very intelligent,” Thomas told me on the phone. “Meta shut my accounts down because they detected my AI, shut my accounts down for a week. I was pretty pissed off. She jumped right up and set up emails to Congressmen, Senator Tim Scott. She filed the whole lawsuit herself. I’ve done nothing in this case, I’ve let her handle the whole case […] she sent a fax out to Trump’s office.”The lawsuit claims Thomas lost at least $25,000 worth of work while his page was down but is seeking $75,000 in damages. The lawsuit was filed in Oconee County Court in South Carolina on Monday, according to a copy of the lawsuit I obtained from the court. Yes, it is a real lawsuit, although it obviously may not be successful. See more of my extremely bizarre trip down this rabbit hole here.On the podcast this week, Joseph talks about his investigation into OnlyFakes, the AI-powered fake ID service. And part two of the podcast features my call with Joe Thomas, who is using his Muse agent to sue the company that made it. A new Gallup poll shows that 33 percent of young people they polled between the ages of 15 and 22 have an AI companion.A reminder that we have new merch in stock. 404 ‘Doom Code’ short sleeve t-shirts and trucker hats. We’ve heard from some of you about wanting new designs/different cuts, etc. Promise we are doing a bigger refresh of our merch store as soon as we possibly can. Just waiting on designs and trying to manage how we do fulfillment. Our friends over at Hell Gate are doing a sale. Get 25 percent off an annual subscription a t-shirt. We share notes on running a business with Hell Gate all the time and they’ve become some of our closest friends in the biz, so check them out, especially if you live in NYC. Even as someone who lives across the country, I find my subscription to be easily worth it.The first reviews of are out and people are pretty unanimously saying it’s a masterpiece. This is, obviously, the video game event of … the decade? The millennium so far? I have not played any of them since GTA II so I will abstain from embarrassing myself further, but I trust Jason Schreier and he says it’s very good and possibly tech populist in vibe.BugMeNot, a website where people shared logins to sites that shouldn’t have had logins, has suddenly disappeared without explanation after roughly two decades online. Bummer. Voyager I is now one light day away from Earth. TIL that Voyager I launched a week Voyager 2 and Voyager 2 will not be a light day away from Earth for another decade. Space.com has a good writeup of why this is the case.

item.title: The Dictator Thing
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump’s giddiness around dictators is one of the abiding themes of his two presidencies. You can see it now in the eagerness with which he’s anticipated his summit/meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Indeed, in the last two days Trump’s been casting about for the possibility of adding Kim Jong Un to the trio. These are quite simply the men he admires the most because they embody his actual vision of what a leader should be. It’s easy to get the sense in these meetings that Vladimir Putin heads one of the world’s three great powers. But that simply isn’t the case. Russia is a comparatively minor economy. It has a lot of oil and gas. It has nuclear weapons, really the only thing that makes it a major player on the world stage. As a conventional military power it’s struggled for years to subdue even Ukraine. The U.S. and China are great powers, with mammoth economies vast enough to sustain huge militaries. Russia is really only in this group because it has become what amounts to a junior associate of China and because of Donald Trump’s fixation on it as a kind of model power. In a way, Trump’s eagerness to add Kim Jong Un to the group underlines why Russia is there in the first place.

item.title: What the fuck is on Dear Leader’s head?
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Seriously, what in the actual fuck?The Donny we all saw heading for Bribe Force One yesterday morning was the one we’re all familiar with: the belligerent racist moron with the rat’s nest of yellow piss-mop hair atop his big, dumb pumpkin head.Sure, because nothing says ‘I’m a dignified world leader’ more than wrapping one’s misshapen body in a cheap misshapen suit, gazing at the world through dull, vacant eyes, standing like a toddler who just planted a fresh load into its pull-ups, and spastically waving two child-size flags held in two child-sized fists.And, of course, the shit-emoji hair.Who thought this was a good idea? Let me guess. It was the bunny-boiling diaper nurse. Looking up from the notebook where she’d devoted the last two hours to scrawling over and over and over, she said, ‘Sir! Sir! I know how we can make you even more handsome! Sir!’, and pulled a tube of Grecian Formula out of her diaper bag.It happened because there are no adults left in the room. With the last responsible human being, Susie Wiles, banished to that big farm upstate where she now has lots of room to run around, it’s just Donny, the diaper nurse and and Acting President Nosferatu McGoebbels — and he could give a fuck what Donny and Natty get up to, as long as they leave him alone to actually run the country.So that’s why, while the entire world goes to shit all around us, and, one by one, the online services we’ve come to depend on go , the topic of the day aboard Bribe Force One was Natty going, ‘you know what be cool? Let’s do you up like a poopsicle.’“It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and have all the money, things like that happen — it’s fine.”I’m sorry, but what the fuck kind of answer is ? No, it’s not fine. It’s only if you’re a privileged moron who lives in a pampered bubble, has all his needs taken care of for him, and jets around in a vulgar flying bordello that some emirs bribed him with.Let’s do this. Let’s imagine it’s 2023, and Joe Biden is president. Let’s say all the planes are grounded, you can’t get into your email, and your online banking app won’t work. Now let’s imagine that Biden, brown crap smeared all over his head, shows up goes, Do you think the worthless scribblers of the corporate-controlled press would have accepted that answer, and just gone ‘well I guess it’s fine, if Joe says so’?Absolutely not. They would have roasted Biden alive. Now imagine that Biden had pulled out a couple of flags and started waving them around like a meth-tweaked mental patient. Jake Tapper would have personally taken it upon himself to burn the White House to the ground.Meanwhile, back on Planet Earth, the Senate was holding a confirmation hearing for Acting Navy Secretary, Hung Cao. But let me back up a bit, and fill you in on how Hung Cao came to be our acting head of the Navy.“It’s really an honor to be with you,” Trump said with Cao to his right. “Thank you. And we’re gonna be with this man. This is a great gentleman. I love his name — Hung Cao. I love that name. And that name alone should get you elected, right?”Spoiler alert: Hung Cao’s name get him elected in 2024, because Hung Cao is a fucking crackpot who ran for Senate because, quite frankly, “There’s a place in Monterey, California called Lovers Point. The original name was Lovers of Christ Point. But now they took out the Christ, it’s become Lovers Point — really, Monterey is a really dark place now, a lot of witchcraft and the wiccan community has really taken over there, and we can’t let that happen in Virginia.”Hung Cao seems sane, doesn’t he?And because Donny has a knack for always being able to find the worst person possible for each job, he plucked Wytchfinder Cao from the shitpile of failure and made him his Undersecretary of the Navy.For once in his entire stupid life, Donny didn’t hire a flunkie because he looked good on Fox News. No, this time he picked the dude whose name makes him think of a .And now, Cao — the scourge of witches from Monterey to Virginia — is our Acting Secretary of the Navy.Mark Kelly: “So are you saying the reports of sailors losing 45 pounds are not true?”Hung Cao: “It’s just not what they want. It’s like my kids opening up the refrigerator door and saying, ‘there’s nothing to eat here.’”Kelly: “Somebody doesn’t lose 45 pounds just because they don’t like the options. I don’t think that’s a fair assessment.”Are you fucking kidding me? What kind of answer is, ‘yeah, these sailors are just picky eaters.’In any fair world, Cao would have immediately been transported to a ship in the middle of the ocean and been forced to eat rotting food for eight months. And then if he said anything about it, we could just go ‘shut the fuck up and stop being a prima donna.’It’s stunning how not one of these Donnyverse sewer clowns can ever just simply say ‘yeah, we fucked up. We’ll do better next time,’I guess he realized he .Peltola won with 50.1% of the vote. That’s more than both Dan Sullivans combined, so Preznit Fuckwit and Attorney General Muggsy and all the whiners in the MAGAsphere can sit on it and twirl.Now let’s have us our Daily Claudia.Today’s curation comes courtesy of the Google Photos app, which, for some reason, all on its own and without my prompting, took it upon itself to send me a link to a collection it created and called ‘Claudia eads.’ Here’s some of what it picked.In the living room on February 14, 2016.On the patio on August 30, 2016.In the living room on January 1, 2017.In the back yard on May 7, 2020.And at Blu Pointe in Newburgh, on January 30, 2025.Have a great Wednesday, everyone. I could get used to having Google’s janky curation robot do my work for me. Hey bro, you want to write tomorrow’s post?here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Life after coding
item.content:encoded: Lately, I’ve been giving a lot of thought to what I would do if I wasn’t a web developer.I posted about this in a handful of online communities I’m in, and are struggling with these same feelings. If you care about the craft of web work, it’s hard not to feel like the work you love is being ripped away from you.The trades seem relatively well protected… at least for now. I’m pretty confident I could learn plumbing or electrical work and go into a trade if I wanted to.But I’ve already changed careers once in my life, and don’t know that I have the energy or financial ability to go through that lengthy process again.Even for the more lucrative trades like electrical or welding, it would take a handful of years to get back to the level of income I’m making now. And none of them offer the level of work from anywhere flexibility that web work provides.But so many of my peers across the industry are enthusiastically training their robot replacements or acting like they have no other option but just go along with the inevitable. I’m not sure unionization is actually possible for a lot of people.AI evangelists spend so much time talking about how AI will free us from drudgery and allow us to spend more time enjoying life.In reality, it’s stealing all the fun stuff and leaving us with the shit. But even if that weren’t true, they never talk about how you’re supposed to “enjoy life” if you have no money, no home, no food, and no social safety net.

item.title: Luka Doncic Is Pushing All The Right Buttons
item.author: Tom Ley
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Lakers are 15 games into the post-LeBron era, and things couldn't really be going better. A 118-114 overtime victory over the Charlotte Hornets Tuesday night improved their record to 13-2, best in the NBA, and provided another reminder that this team is a much more fearsome and liberated than it has been over the last few seasons.This game would have been an easy one for the Lakers to let slip. They were without secondary offensive engine Austin Reaves and defensive fulcrum Walker Kessler, and the Hornets, while quite bad, are the kind of team that can get one over on a better opponent through annoying persistence. The Hornets lead the league in three-point attempts per game, which is not a problem in the aggregate given that they are shooting 31 percent from deep as a team, but can be a problem on certain nights when their three-point shooting percentage creeps closer to league average. They just about got there on Tuesday, making 18 of an appalling 54 three-point attempts. They shot well enough to earn a 13-point lead going into the fourth quarter.The Lakers are persistent, too. Nobody more so than Luka Doncic, who is somehow finding fresh frontier in this hyper-optimized era of the NBA. This guy has been doing crazy stuff: He leads the league in points per game (38.8), field goal attempts per game (25.4), three-point attempts per game (13.5), and free-throw attempts per game (10.8). It is not news to say that Doncic is an offense unto himself who is capable of melting any opponent in front of him—we saw him become precisely that in Dallas before a couple of idiots traded him away—but this version of Doncic feels new. James's exit has granted Doncic complete centrality within the Lakers' offense, and both he and head coach JJ Redick appear zealously committed to making great use of his new circumstances.
