item.title: Trump says I should go to jail
item.author: 1axbtgroo9jlo0q00k7zsvogooq1j45ibhesbn@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: The United States is in the midst of a constitutional crisis. I do not make this claim lightly or with any intended hyperbole. I am saying it now because too few are willing to speak out. If we fail to recognize it for what it is, it will only get worse.Despite what we want to believe about what is “normal,” for the last decade, United States elections have been held hostage. We live under threat that one major party will not accept the results.The president uses his power to target vote counting and certification. He deploys federal prosecutors to intimidate opposition figures.If this were another country, would we not agree that it faces a constitutional crisis? Would we say the crisis is over because the sitting president and his party failed in their efforts to subvert the midterm elections?I understand that mine is not a popular opinion.Those on the right want to act as if Donald Trump’s actions have been justified all along. Many on the left want to celebrate the midterms as if the threat has been defeated. Much of the legacy media sees its role as questioning whether the crisis ever existed at all.To be clear, litigating election rules and contesting election results does not by itself create a constitutional crisis.A constitutional crisis occurs when those who hold power systematically weaponize the machinery of government against the very institutions the Constitution relies on to check that power. At a minimum, those checks include free and fair elections, equal treatment under the law and respect for democratic outcomes.This is an intentionally narrow definition. Even after Jan. 6, 2021, I did not view the 2020 election as a crisis of constitutional dimensions.As despicable as his actions were, Trump was acting largely as a defeated candidate. The scores of lawsuits filed by him and his allies relied on private resources. When he pressed the Department of Justice to intervene, its leadership refused.In the end, the federal government did not become an instrument for altering the results. Trump considered a draft executive order in December 2020 that would have directed the Pentagon to seize voting machines, but he ultimately did not sign it.The threats to the 2026 midterms were far more serious, because this time the government itself was the instrument.It was the DOJ, not GOP campaigns, that tried to coerce states to turn over their sensitive voter data. It was by executive orders that Trump tried to tamper with state voting laws and weaponize the U.S. Postal Service. It was at the president’s direction that the DOJ tried to block the certification of a Democrat in the Alaska Senate race.Most troubling has been the increased abuse of criminal law to threaten election officials and political opponents. These tactics began before the election. It was the FBI, under Kash Patel, that seized Fulton County, Georgia’s 2020 ballots and election records in January 2026.But they have continued and escalated ever since.I know this firsthand. I have spent my career representing Democrats in election litigation. That work has resulted in handing scores of defeats to Trump and Republicans in cases involving close elections.In 2020, I helped lead the litigation to defeat Trump and his allies more than 60 times. In the run-up to this election, my law firm defeated Trump’s DOJ more than 30 times in court.Only days before Election Day, it was revealed that Trump’s DOJ considered me a target of a criminal probe involving the Alaska Senate race. That designation came notwithstanding the U.S. Attorney saying that he wasn’t certain if there was any crime committed by anyone.That did not matter to Trump. In the days that followed, the president repeatedly said on national television and on social media that I should go to jail.After initially saying he would accept the results, Trump backtracked and suggested they were rigged.When congressional Democrats made clear they would conduct oversight, Trump announced he was ordering the Justice Department to look into it. His White House counsel then warned that their investigative plans could cross into criminal behavior.Critics of my argument will point out that no 2026 ballots were seized, no federal law enforcement appeared at the polls and Democrats won resounding victories. They will note that those results are being certified at the state level, and there is no indication that the peaceful transfer of power in Congress on Jan. 3, 2027, will not take place.Above all, they will point out that the courts largely reined in the president’s actions and that their orders were followed.Such a myopic view confuses Trump’s actions with the election results. Voters can overcome an abuse of power, but that does not make it any less an abuse.With the help of the courts, voters may have defeated the attacks on our elections, but that does not diminish the attacks’ significance. And these claims ignore what is continuing to happen.A bank teller who foils a robbery is still the victim of a crime. And if more robberies continue to occur at other banks, the spree has not ended.The question is not whether Trump’s efforts succeeded. It is whether the executive branch went along with them and continues to do so.Some pundits will say that I am raising a false alarm, that all of this shows how strong our elections are and that the system of protecting against government abuses has worked. But this misses the point.Courts are imperfect protectors of democracy. They can block only what has already been attempted, and only after someone sues. A system that survives only by winning dozens of emergency lawsuits or by the falsely accused being exonerated at trial is neither healthy nor sustainable.Now that voters have handed Congress to the Democrats, we are seeing an escalation of, not a retreat from, Trump’s attacks on the Constitution. His administration is systematically targeting congressional oversight.Perhaps Democratic officials will remain strong in the face of these threats. Will the same be true of the staff and witnesses who make oversight possible?I have grown accustomed to being targeted by Trump. But how many other lawyers will shy away from taking on the administration if the threat of prosecution is the cost of doing the work?If all of this were happening in another country, we would know what to call it. A country whose leader turned the full force of the government he controls against its own elections, his political opponents and congressional leaders would not be considered a normal democracy.It would be described as a democracy in crisis. If it had a robust constitution, it would be called a constitutional crisis. We should be willing to say the same about our own.Calling this crisis what it is will allow us to do something about it. It will empower the courts to protect democracy. It will encourage Congress to assert its power, conduct oversight over the administration and enact needed reforms.Most importantly, recognizing that we are in a constitutional crisis will allow us to fully and finally commit to defeating the threat Trump has posed over the last decade, and the threat his movement poses in the years ahead.

item.title: Flow State Episode 352: Neo-Krautrock
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today’s mix is a collection of “neo-krautrock” music, off the back of Friday’s recommendation of Fling II. Krautrock formed in the ‘60s and ‘70s in Germany, defined by bands such as Neu!, Harmonia, Can, and (early) Kraftwerk. It influenced the post-punk and post-rock scenes in Britain and the U.S. across later decades, and in recent years several indie bands have revived the style. Many infuse outside influences such as minimalism, kosmische (krautrock’s synthesizer-forward cousin), and techno. Today’s neo-krautrock mix is mostly guitar/rock music, bands like Papir, Tross, Acid Rooster, Motor!k, Lüger, and Kombynat Robotron. A couple more kosmische-style tracks appear by Kosmischer Läufer, Trees Speak, and Seconds. The mix concludes with a track by Time Wharp and CH Rom, from an album fittingly called Radical American Hippy Kraut0:00:00 - Kosmischer Läufer - Siegerehrung / Abschied von der Zukunft0:05:23 - Oren Ambarchi, Johan Berthling & Andreas Werliin - Shesh

item.title: Is Netanyahu Feeding Trump Scary Iran Intel In a Desperate Bid to Remain in Power?
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: CNN just published a story claiming that U.S. intelligence had picked up evidence that Iran may be planning a dirty bomb or chemical weapons attack in Washington, D.C., targeting top administration officials. They make no mention of Israel or Israeli intelligence, but if you’re following news out of Israel since the October 27th election, you’ll know that Benjamin Netanyahu has been working in overdrive to get the U.S. to restart the hot war with Iran, apparently believing that a renewed conflict will give him leverage to remain in power. There were similar efforts just before the election. The aim then was to perhaps delay the election as a war-time measure.For the last several days the Israeli press has been talking about how Netanyahu’s government has been telling the U.S. it has intel on possible Iranian attacks on top Cabinet officials as well on Trump himself. This comes as the opposition bloc has been warning Netanyahu not to take any steps to restart fighting while Gadi Eisenkot works to form a “change” government unless a military action is based on some concrete imminent threat. They clearly think he’s going to try to do that. And the Chief of Staff of the IDF has apparently already resisted pressure to back such action.

item.content:encoded: A bug fix release for LLM, mainly to cover a problem with the most recent Homebrew package of the software.Short version: in SQLite 3.54.0 the following SQL:select json_object('a', (select json_array(1))) But in 3.54.1 the same query returns this:That was a bug fix. Per the documentation, (SELECT json_array(...)) returns SQL text, not JSON. Hence the 3.54.1 behavior is correct and 3.54.0 was a bug.The workaround looks like this:select json_object('a', json((select json_array(1))))

item.title: Crime and Punishment in America
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Documentary filmmaker Lynn Novick, who co-directed The Vietnam War and The US and the Holocaust with Ken Burns, has directed an 8-hour PBS series called Crime and Punishment in America.A sweeping look at the American criminal justice system, from the origins of prisons and policing to our continued fascination with crime, the film traces the contours of our imperfect system and how it influences nearly all parts of our society: the media, economics and politics. Through the voices and testimony of those who have committed crimes, experienced incarceration, enforced the law, or lost loved ones to violence, the series explores the cost of America’s choices and the enduring tension between crime and punishment, vengeance and mercy, justice and redemption.We think about our history in terms of progress, but we have become consumed with practices of punishment.When I think about crime and punishment in America, I think that it says we are a very unforgiving country.This looks great. It starts airing on PBS tonight, Nov 16.

item.title: Waiting For Jensen
item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: "Excuse me, can you move so I can take a photo?" a woman asked me and my friend Adam, referring to the large plaque above us bearing seven photos and an inscription: The Booth That Launched A Multi-Trillion-Dollar Company. How could we deny a fellow pilgrim this humble reliquary? We were all here on this rainy Sunday evening to feel the weight of history settle lightly on our shoulders, and also to have some pancakes. We shuffled out into the otherwise empty room while she took a couple pictures, her solemn bearing occasionally quivering out into a quarter of a grin.For Steve Jobs, inspiration struck in the garage at 2066 Crist Drive in Los Altos. For Mark Zuckerberg, there was Room H33 at Harvard's Kirkland House Dorm. For Jensen Huang and his Nvidia co-founders, it all started at the Denny's at 2484 Berryessa Road in San Jose, specifically the big booth in the far corner.Those looking to get closer to the Huang story have few options. You'll have a hard time founding a $4 trillion company, cheating on Jensen Huang's wife, or unwittingly passing on sensitive information to the Chinese government via a mysterious business executive. You have to go back to the beginning. Before Huang was the load-bearing joist propping up the American stock market and an alleged disgrace to the leather jacket community, he was simply a tech worker kicking around Silicon Valley during the first boom. The foundational myth of Nvidia, and by extension Huang, is grounded in the mundane social reality of life in Silicon Valley in some critical ways.

item.title: Elderly Dog Benefits From Pilates
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Weasel is an almost 16-year-old golden retriever in Hawaii. That's an advanced age, especially for a big dog. His family wanted to do anything they could to help him, and started Weasel on physical therapy. His human Jillian is a pilates instructor, so she started taking him to her studio for gentle workouts. And Weasel showed that his 16 years brought him a lot of smarts even as it was taking his physical strength- he copied her moves! Jillian calls these workouts "paw-lates."Progress was slow, but it was progress, as the dog gained strength and flexibility. And while his face is still white, he now has the mobility of a much younger dog- most of the time. He still needs a little help every now and then, but don't we all? You can see more of Weasel's fitness journey at Instagram.

item.title: ‘Paranormal Activity’ On Broadway Has Some Good Scares, But Not Much Else
item.author: Nicholas Russell
item.content:encoded: It’s hard to overstate just how absurd we thought the whole thing was, even as we purchased tickets and organized getting to the theater. A play. a musical, I stressed, though my friends and I kept laughing at how funny that idea seemed. I don’t live in New York and am therefore distant from its many stage sensations, though I’ve been hearing about movies and TV shows, well-known IP, popping up on Broadway for years. I remember when the musical premiered with Doctor Who (Matt Smith) in the starring role in London in 2013, when they turned into a play the year before. I was particularly taken with the musical as a teenager, though less so with the musical that added more contemporary songs to the jukebox. Last year, Stranger Things: The First Shadow made its way to New York from the UK, a whirlwind of impressive special effects and basically nothing else.Then Instagram ads for populated my feed in late August. I thought maybe a nationwide rescreening was being teased for Halloween. It’s been almost 20 years since the first installment came out, so why not? But I’d missed the tag that read “A New Story Live on Broadway” until a close friend whose critical opinion I value said she was going to see it. I’m an evangelist for the third movie, but that’s only because I’m an evangelist for the found-footage form, and that film’s admittedly dumb but effective scares are still some of my favorites.

item.title: What Robert Caro Has Learned About Power
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Dwarkesh Patel recently interviewed Robert Caro for his podcast. They talked about loneliness, if JFK could have passed LBJ’s legislation, and how Caro gets people to talk. From the transcript:Dwarkesh Patel: This raises another question that I wanted to ask you. You’re interviewing all these people, and in many cases, they must know that it’s not good for them to tell you what you want to know. In many cases, they tell you anyway. How do you get people to tell you things that they know they shouldn’t tell you?Robert Caro: You ask terrific questions. Sometimes you’re sitting there and you know this person doesn’t want to talk to you about what you want to get out of them, like John Connally on how Johnson used money to get political power. I’m thinking, “But I’ve been through the notes. Connally collected the money and gave it out at Johnson’s instructions, so he’s the only guy who can tell me how Johnson did this, how he judged who to give money to.”Sometimes Johnson would write on a request for money. If the guy asked for $1,500, Johnson would write, “Okay, 1,500.” Sometimes he’d write 500, sometimes he’d write no, but sometimes he’d write, “No, never.” I asked Connally what that meant, and he said, “This guy was never going to get money from Lyndon Johnson.” Then when you ask why he felt this way about this particular congressman, that’s when the really fascinating stories emerge.Caro is 91 now, so every interview with him is a precious jewel, but one wonders if he’s got the time to finish that fifth LBJ book.

item.title: Let Trump Own Every Bit of the Disasters He’s Created
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: This is the first edition of Unsanctioned, the weekday newsletter formerly known as Morning Memo. Unsanctioned will continue chronicling the historic threats and deep absurdities of the late-stage Trump era.For longtime readers, I explained last week what will change and what will remain the same from its predecessor Morning Memo. New readers who want to receive Unsanctioned via email can sign up for free.I’m glad you’re all here. Let’s get to it.Setting the Post-Election SceneWe’re in a particularly weird interregnum between the historic midterm elections and the new Democratic-controlled Congress taking power in January — but get used to it because much of the weirdness is likely to persist through the 2028 election.With an erratic lame-duck GOP president largely insulated from the political winds of the moment but eager to wield his veto power, the next two years on the Hill are going to be largely about containing him and mitigating further damage. The remaining balance of the political and legislative work will be spent on setting the stage for winning a Democratic trifecta in 2028, at which point the real work of undoing the worst of the Trump II damage and getting the country back on track can begin.But as the events of the last few days showed with remarkable clarity, the world continues to spin in accelerated fashion thanks to Trump II. Whether it’s a nationwide FAA outage (thoughts with readers stranded over the weekend), a high-flying AI CEO brought low by a honeypot, the threats of climate change, or the revocation of the U.S.’s measles elimination status, events aren’t going to wait until the United States gets its politics sorted and shores up its democracy.Expectations among Democratic partisans continue to be way out of whack given the limitations of even hefty majorities in both chambers — expectations only exceeded by the chronic hand-wringing that elected Democrats are going to screw it all up and squander the opportunity.Foremost among the misplaced expectations is that Democrats should project some main character energy so that we can finally shuffle the narcissistic president off his mark at center stage. But absent the ravages of old age taking a sudden and unexpected toll, Trump isn’t going anywhere for the next two years — and the Constitution does, for better or worse, vest main character energy in the president. Given the current economic and political landscape, that’s just fine.Why would Democrats willingly shoulder the yoke of cleaning up Trump’s colossal mess when they didn’t create it and don’t yet have the power to fix it?Be skeptical anytime anyone says Democrats “must” do this or “have to” do that. Democrats have maximum flexibility and maneuvering room for the next year and half. They’re not bound to do any one thing, including rescuing Trump from himself. They can do everything or nothing. They can pick and choose. They can leave Trump dangling in the wind.Don’t let Trump off the hook by overstating Democrats’ power to rein him in. He is an ongoing disaster, and voters saw it clearly for what it was. He will spend the next two years flailing just as spectacularly — while Democratic oversight will likely uncover new and even more dire examples of the disaster that was the last two years. Republicans in competitive races in 2028 — including the presidential candidates — will be trapped looking for any way to simultaneously run away from Trump and shift the blame to Democrats for the Trump catastrophe. It’s a very strong position for Democrats to be in.Brian Beutler: “A new project, spearheaded by veterans of the Obama and Biden administrations, should hearten those of us who are concerned the Democratic Party will return to power in 2029 unprepared to build a functioning government atop the wreckage of the Trump regime.”“I don’t think we should play this game where the things we want have to be paid for and the things they want can be put on a credit card. So I’m cautious about falling into that trap, but if we can find pay-fors, that’s even better.”—Sen. Brian Schatz (D-HI), confronting the long-running double standard that the GOP can spend like drunken sailors when in power while Democrats must exercise fiscal restraint when they win: At the last minute, U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a temporary restraining order late Saturday blocking the Trump administration from closing East Potomac Park in D.C. as scheduled on Sunday. But she stopped short of ordering the administration to keep the East Potomac Golf Course in operation — and it has now shut down. Trump has vowed to appeal.: Anna Bower on the new revelations about how far the Trump DOJ has been willing to go to vindictively prosecute former FBI Director James Comey: Marcy Wheeler on the DOJ’s ploy to keep line prosecutors off the stand as U.S. District Judge April Perry investigates potential contempt of courtMust Read on Boat StrikesWaPo: “A high-tech surveillance plane that repeatedly flew in the vicinity of CIA-linked attacks on boats near the Galápagos Islands this year had an unlikely first owner: a company based in The Villages, the retirement mega-community in Florida.”What a Difference Two Years MakeAt this point in 2024, Reps. Lauren Boebert (R-CO), Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA), and Rep. Matt Gaetz (R-FL) had just been re-elected to Congress, and Gaetz was President Trump’s announced pick for attorney general.Within weeks, Gaetz wasn’t just out of the running for attorney general, he resigned his seat and was out of Congress. Greene likewise resigned, earlier this year. And with Boebert’s defeat in this year’s election now official, the entire MAGA squad will be gone come January.

item.title: Aidan Hutchinson Ended The Patriots’ Season, And Then His Own, On One Play
item.author: Luis Paez-Pumar
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Lions beat the reeling New England Patriots, 35-10, in Munich on Sunday. The new NFC North leaders put up almost 500 total yards on offense, with half-German Amon-Ra St. Brown scoring twice on four catches and Jahmyr Gibbs continuing to make his "best player in football" case with 252 total yards and two touchdowns. It was a great win for the Lions, except for one play that simultaneously took out two stars and might have altered the course of the season for both teams.On New England's first drive of the game, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson got through beleaguered Pats left tackle Will Campbell and took a wide-open angle at quarterback Drake Maye, who couldn't do anything but take a sack and protect the ball. What he couldn't protect, though, was his right ankle, which got caught at an odd angle on the Munich grass. Hutchinson, meanwhile, celebrated his sixth sack of the season, running about 10 yards away and jumping into the air for a fist pump.That's when everything went to shit. Hutchinson landed awkwardly on his right leg and immediately crumpled to the ground in pain. Detroit's team doctors ran out to check on him as he held onto his right knee. He left the game and eventually returned to the locker room.

item.title: AI-Powered Copyright Hell
item.author: Jason Koebler
item.content:encoded: Happy Monday, everybody. We hope you didn't get stranded this weekend. This is looking to be quite a busy week, what with the tech-related airplane grounding and all. To get things started, we have a story from Matthew Gault about a human singer whose work got caught in an AI-generated copyright hell.When writer and musician Samantha Shokin noticed her cover of a public domain Bulgarian folk song had been copyright struck on YouTube, she assumed it would be easy to fix. It wasn’t. And trying to figure out what happened led her to discover an AI content mill that is running 500 slop-filled channels and abusing YouTube’s automated copyright detectors.“Any human would agree with me that there’s something clearly wrong here that needs to be fixed, but I can’t get in touch with a human being,” Shokin said.Shokin’s journey is a modern nightmare that highlights the ways AI can be weaponized against human creators, and the ways people fall through the cracks of big tech’s automated systems.During the pandemic, Shokin recorded a 50 second version of the Bulgarian folk song ‘Bre Petrunko’ and uploaded it to SoundCloud, where it didn’t get much traction. Two years later, she uploaded it to YouTube and watched as her cover grew in popularity, gaining 125,000 views in four years.Last summer, she noticed an uptick in comments on the video. Unbeknownst to Shokin, her version of “Bre Petruinko” had become popular among DJs and electronic artists and had been sampled in dozens of songs. Someone in the comments pointed her towards one of the more popular tracks. “I look up this video and it’s something that has millions of hits [...] and 30 seconds into this track I hear my own voice and I was utterly shocked. I didn’t know how to react,” she said (the video has more than 4 million views).“The first thing that comes to mind is, ‘Oh my god, someone stole my voice and didn’t credit me,’” she said. Shokin said she talked to a lot of DJs and figured out how they’d gotten her voice. They’d purchased a pack of samples from a company called Loopmasters that was selling her version of “Bre Petruinko” as part of its “Folk Legends” set.“I got in touch with the distributor and they were deeply apologetic. They were unaware that this had happened and they immediately tried to make right of the situation and granted me royalties on the sample pack,” Shokin said. “At that point, countless DJs and music producers had been using my voice for their own tracks, unbeknownst to me. At least I’m aware and at least I was making something off of it and I was satisfied with that. I didn’t love the way that it came about, but whatever, they tried to make right of the situation.”But Shokin’s “Bre Petruinko” saga wasn’t over. Last month, she opened YouTube and noticed her original recording was gone. A company called Media Nov Records had issued a copyright strike against her song, and YouTube had taken it down. She thought it would be easy to get this reversed. It’s a public domain folk song and she had the original recordings and a history with a distributor. “If I just explain it to YouTube, they’ll understand,” she thought.Media Nov Records advertises itself as a “distribution company” that that partners with artists to release their music on digital platforms. But a lot of its website focuses on rights management and copyright protection. “At Media Nov, we go above and beyond to safeguard your musical creations. Our comprehensive rights management system leverages cutting-edge technology and legal expertise to ensure you receive the royalties you deserve,” it said on its website.YouTube uses automated systems to work through copyright claims. When someone files a claim against a video, the company tends to automatically approve it. The original uploader can file a “counterclaim,” where they argue that the video should stay up, or that it should not be demonetized.Shokin filed two counterclaims, but neither worked. “It's unclear to us whether you have a valid reason for filing a counter notification, so we won't be able to honor your request,” YouTube said in its last denial. It told her to contact the copyright holder; in this case, it was a public domain song and so there was no actual “copyright holder,” just Media Nov, which was claiming to hold it.“I tried emailing them,” she said. “I tried calling them. There doesn’t appear to be a working phone line. I got in touch with [Loopmaster, which was selling her recording]. They tried getting in touch. I’m being ignored by everybody, by YouTube, by this media company that, like, the website seems to be entirely AI-generated, and all I want is to talk to a human about this.”This Comic Kills Technofascists: We had a wonderful Q&A from our friend Dave Maass over the weekend about , Laura Hudson’s new comic about independent journalists who take on technofascists. We’ll be experimenting here and there with more tech culture coverage so let us know what you’re intoIn the interview pod this week, Matt talks to Ankit Panda, author of , about how AI is affecting how experts consider nuclear war and the nuclear threat more broadly. We have some new merch! We finally made our very popular 404 ‘Doom Code’ tank tops and long sleeve shirts in short sleeve t-shirt form. Now available in all sleeve configurations. And we’ve now got a trucker hat, too. We’re slowly working our way through redoing our merch, so expect some new designs in the coming weeks, though probably not in time for the holidays (oops). Everyone I know has asked me about the FAA’s ground stop Friday, and has asked what happened and if I’m going to report on it. By the time the ground stop was issued, I had felt like I’d gotten hit by a bus, so the answer was basically: I don’t know and I’m going to bed! And that sort of seems to be the case for our administration, which insists this has nothing to do with AI and as of the time I’m writing this does not seem to have a definitive explanation for what happened, says no one is going to lose their jobs over this, and whose communication strategy has mainly seemed to be standing at a podium and yelling at people who are annoyed by the mass chaos of having every flight grounded. I’m not sure if we’ll have more coverage on this or not, but wow, what a mess. As of this morning, it’s looking like we’re blaming a router in Arkansas, which is now being studying in a “lab down in Florida,” the administration said. We have done some stuff in the part with flight tracking and have ambiently learned that our air traffic control system is a mess and the actual workers are exhausted, but unfortunately we’re not super well-sourced in this space. So we’ll keep an eye out, probably send some FOIAs, but not sure if we’ll be able to break any new ground here. As an emo, though, I must say I was thrilled to see the Hoobastank/Simple Plan/The Used Southwest Airlines mid-flight concert, then annoyed to learn it was a Warped Tour psy-op. A federal judge in California denied a motion to dismiss a class-action lawsuit against Micro, Samsung, and SK hynix that accuses them of collaborating to jack up the price of RAM, which has increased in price more than 500% in the last year or so as manufacturers pivot to selling to AI data centers rather than consumers. Speaking of jacked up prices, I was yammering in here the other day about how expensive Raspberry Pi prices have gotten. I enjoyed this blog about using an old phone as a Raspberry Pi stand-in instead. Used Android phones are pretty cheap. It’s a great idea.Google’s elite hacking team Project Zero says that in an effort to push software developers to patch their stuff faster, it will reduce the amount of time it gives them to fix a vulnerability before disclosing it to the public. Google says “vulnerabilities will be disclosed 90 days after they are reported to the vendor,” that early next year it will move to a 60-day policy, and that in 2028 it will move to a 30 day policy because “LLMs have increased the speed at which attackers can find and exploit vulnerabilities.” It also says “LLMs have also increased the volume of vulnerabilities that Project Zero reports. We are finding several vulnerabilities a week in targets where we once found a few vulnerabilities a year,” and that “Aspects of our policy that require vendor negotiation or agreement, including determining whether a bug is fixed and whether grace period applies, are quickly becoming unmanageable.”

item.title: Dear Leader’s not dead yet. In fact, he’s feeling much better.
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Loyal and patriotic citizens, once again we must ask you to please stand by for a message of the utmost importance from the President of the United States, Supreme Ruler of the Western Hemisphere, Lord-Emperor of the Sky Above and All the Planets, Conqueror Of Every War, God’s Own Avatar on Earth, Grand Re-namer of Water, Master Builder of Vulgar Dance Halls and the Pants-Shittingest Moron to Ever Crap Himself In the Oval Bordello.“I am in the White House having meetings on many subjects. Very exciting times for the USA. Great things are happening - We are the “hottest” Country anywhere in the World! President DJT”Oh my god. This fragile, easily-triggered bottomless well of dipshit need took the bait. He couldn’t leave it alone. He heard all the chatter on the socials about ‘where’s Donny? We haven’t seen him for days. Is he dead?’And so Preznit Fuckwit just couldn’t help himself. He just had to fart out some patently false, ‘I’m having many meetings on many subjects. You don’t know the people I’m meeting with. They go to a different school, in Canada.’ Does Donny seriously have no idea what a fool he’s making of himself? Everyone knows he’s not having ‘many meetings on many subjects.’ He’s been on some IV drip, or playing patty-cake with Natty while watching himself on TV.‘I’m not dead yet. In fact. I’m feeling much better. I think I’ll go for a walk.’You’re not fooling anyone.He’s such an embarrassment. MAGA, how the fuck are you not ashamed to have hitched your wagon to this unserious goofball?Anyway, we’re going to get plenty of proof of life from Donny this week. Way too much proof of lifeToday, Donny heads to the Philippines, where tomorrow he’s taking part in a meeting of ‘the Quad’ — the leaders of US, Japan, Australia and India. So you know what that means: breathless coverage of Donny dementedly weaving across tarmacs, waving to imaginary crowds, and falling asleep in his chair while crop-dusting the President of Japan.If we’re really lucky, we’ll get to watch Dear Leader wander past the open door of his limo, as his security detail tries desperately — and without success — to lure him back to reality.Who thought this was a good idea?Oh sure, let’s take an 80-year-old demento in cognitive collapse, fly him halfway across the world, so he gets good and disoriented, and sit him down with two homies who are both smarter and craftier than he is. What could possibly go wrong?If we’re lucky, all that will happen is that our narcoleptic fart-factory president will immediately pass out, leaving Xi and Putin to marinate in the pungent aroma of Donny’s ass music.Worst case, Preznit Fuckwit gives away the store, gets taken to the cleaners, and sells out our allies.If Donny’s minders and flunkies gave a shit about the United States, or our allies, or anyone at all but their own corrupt, greedy selves, they would not be allowing this meeting between Donny and his despot besties to take place.Donny should be confined to the White House, when he can canoodle to his heart’s content with the diaper nurse, while pretending to have If Congress approves the desperately needed money for Air Traffic Control, we can get it built quickly and efficiently. It will be the BEST SYSTEM anywhere in the World. Much of our current air control system is 50 years old - RIDICULOUS! We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs. Congress must approve. The Biden Administration set it back years! President DJTDonny’s trying to pin this all on Joe Biden, because . That’s his signature move whenever shit goes sideways. Sleepy Joe Biden, blah blah blah. Fuck straight off with this fever-swamp fairy tale, Donny.NEWS: Trump Was Warned About Air Traffic Control RisksA group of aviation experts warned in 2023 that rushing the modernization of air traffic control systems was risky. In 2024, the Biden Administration asked the same group to look at air traffic control safety issues.Trump disbanded the group in 2025.Got that? Joe Biden was advised that our nation’s air traffic control system was in serious need of upgrading, and he did what any responsible leader would do — he set forth to make it happen. But then Donny slithered his slimy way back into office, immediately decided we didn’t need that shit, and disbanded Biden’s air traffic task force.If any of that sounds familiar, it should, because back in 2016, Obama left Donny with a detailed, 69-page plan about what do to if we ever had a pandemic — and Donny was all ‘why the fuck would I want this?’ Tell me, how did the lack of a plan work out for us, when covid took everyone by surprise? Instead of an actual expertise, we had a moron telling us to gargle horse paste and inject bleach.In September, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) warned that the Trump Administration’s modernization approach prioritized “speed at the risk of cost uncertainty and potential disruptions.”Now we’re seeing why those warnings mattered. The rush to replace the system before Trump leaves office is causing chaos and putting lives at risk.Modernizing our aging air traffic control system is essential. But you can’t just rip out old technology, install new equipment, and hope for the best.Do you remember what Sean Duffy spent his summer doing? Spoiler alert: he wasn’t working on an air traffic control plan. If you recall, he spent seven months filming a reality show that no one ended up watching.Good use of everyone’s time, am I right? Maybe we should all be gargling horse paste right now. Maybe that’ll keep the planes in the air. Could guzzling goo be any worse than Duffy’s actual plan, which involves giving a no-bid contract to a crony, and then hastily installing whatever janky crap they shit out, without first properly testing it?Here’s a fun fact: transportation secretaries can be impeached, you know. Congress needs to investigate what went wrong, and determine what safeguards are needed to prevent more damage from being done.January 3rd. It’s just 48 days from today. Let’s hope these dumbfucks don’t break everything all to hell before then.I know, this sounds like the winner of a make-up-the-dumbest-sounding-scandal-you-canFoundation Future Industries, a maker of military humanoid robots advised and backed by Eric Trump, failed to pay employees last month as its cash reserves dwindled, according to people with direct knowledge of the matter.Workers have yet to receive paychecks after San Francisco-based Foundation missed payroll on Oct. 30, said the people, who asked for anonymity to speak candidly about a private company.The situation has particularly angered some inside the startup because its CEO and co-founder, Sankaet Pathak, borrowed $4.6 million from the company last year to buy a luxury home, money that could have been used to pay workers, the people said.How is it that everything that Donny or one of his felonious failsons gets their fingers on, ends up being tainted by scandal? You would imagine that every now and then, they’d fall ass-backwards into doing something honest, just by accident — but no. Everything — no matter what it is — ended up being some kind of fly-by-night grift.Fucking hell, now it’s .You can’t make this shit up, because who would believe it?Now let’s have us our Daily Claudia.Here are two shots of Ms Spouse I found while scrolling through her Facebook page. This one’s from the 1980s, at her bff Mandi’s apartment.This next one’s from the 2000s. I don’t recognize the location, and Ms Spouse was terrible at captioning the stuff she put up on Facebook. Have a great Monday, everyone. here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Techlords and Billionaires Mobilize for Jensen Huang Restoration
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: It’s not clear to me that this will go anywhere. And I don’t want to hang too much on one decision of corporate governance. But a fascinating and, I think, pretty significant development occurred over the weekend in the Silicon Valley tech world — or, more specifically, a development that’s tied to Silicon Valley’s rapid turn to the right. Their argument is that the problem isn’t whatever Huang did, but rather, it’s that he didn’t sufficiently control his board. Because he didn’t, they were able to force him to resign.This isn’t as crazy as it sounds. There’s a big contingent in Silicon Valley that believes companies should operate in “founder mode.” And a lot of big tech companies especially are structured in a way as to guarantee the control of founders even though they control only a small percentage of equity in the company. Still, boards are a central feature of corporate governance, even though they are often dominated by powerful CEOs. They should either exist or they shouldn’t.

item.title: How an AI Content Mill Put a Real Musician Through Copyright Hell
item.author: Matthew Gault
item.content:encoded: When writer and musician Samantha Shokin noticed her cover of a public domain Bulgarian folk song had been copyright struck on YouTube, she assumed it would be easy to fix. It wasn’t. And trying to figure out what happened led her to discover an AI content mill that is running 500 slop-filled channels and abusing YouTube’s automated copyright detectors.“Any human would agree with me that there’s something clearly wrong here that needs to be fixed, but I can’t get in touch with a human being,” Shokin said.Shokin’s journey is a modern nightmare that highlights the ways AI can be weaponized against human creators, and the ways people fall through the cracks of big tech’s automated systems.During the pandemic, Shokin recorded a 50 second version of the Bulgarian folk song ‘Bre Petrunko’ and uploaded it to , where it didn’t get much traction. Two years later, she and watched as her cover grew in popularity, gaining 125,000 views in four years.Last summer, she noticed an uptick in comments on the video. Unbeknownst to Shokin, her version of “Bre Petruinko” had become popular among DJs and electronic artists and had been sampled in dozens of songs. Someone in the comments pointed her towards one of the more popular tracks. “ and it’s something that has millions of hits [...] and 30 seconds into this track I hear my own voice and I was utterly shocked. I didn’t know how to react,” she said (the video has more than 4 million views).“The first thing that comes to mind is, ‘Oh my god, someone stole my voice and didn’t credit me,’” she said. Shokin said she talked to a lot of DJs and figured out how they’d gotten her voice. They’d purchased a pack of samples from a company called Loopmasters that was selling her version of “Bre Petruinko” as part of its .“I got in touch with the distributor and they were deeply apologetic. They were unaware that this had happened and they immediately tried to make right of the situation and granted me royalties on the sample pack,” Shokin said. “At that point, countless DJs and music producers had been using my voice for their own tracks, unbeknownst to me. At least I’m aware and at least I was making something off of it and I was satisfied with that. I didn’t love the way that it came about, but whatever, they tried to make right of the situation.”But Shokin’s “Bre Petruinko” saga wasn’t over. Last month, she opened YouTube and noticed her original recording was gone. A company called Media Nov Records had issued a copyright strike against her song, and YouTube had taken it down.She thought it would be easy to get this reversed. It’s a public domain folk song and she had the original recordings and a history with a distributor. “If I just explain it to YouTube, they’ll understand,” she thought.Media Nov Records advertises itself as a “distribution company” that that partners with artists to release their music on digital platforms. But a focuses on rights management and copyright protection. “At Media Nov, we go above and beyond to safeguard your musical creations. Our comprehensive rights management system leverages cutting-edge technology and legal expertise to ensure you receive the royalties you deserve,” it said on its website.YouTube uses automated systems to work through copyright claims. When someone files a claim against a video, the company tends to automatically approve it. The original uploader can file a “counterclaim,” where they argue that the video should stay up, or that it should not be demonetized.Shokin filed two counterclaims, but neither worked. “It's unclear to us whether you have a valid reason for filing a counter notification, so we won't be able to honor your request,” YouTube said in its last denial. It told her to contact the copyright holder; in this case, it was a public domain song and so there was no actual “copyright holder,” just Media Nov, which was claiming to hold it.“I tried emailing them,” she said. “I tried calling them. There doesn’t appear to be a working phone line. I got in touch with [Loopmaster, which was selling her recording]. They tried getting in touch. I’m being ignored by everybody, by YouTube, by this media company that, like, the website seems to be entirely AI-generated, and all I want is to talk to a human about this.”Media Nov’s site boasted about its use of automated DMCA takedowns, YouTube content ID management, and AI-powered content recognition. “Our advanced AI identifies your music across platforms ensuring accurate tracking and protection,” it said. The company says it has been in existence since 1996, but ’s Wayback Machine doesn’t show much of a web presence until last year. Its website is basic and barebones. The company has two addresses on its website. One is an apartment building in Los Angeles on Marina Del Rey. The other is the Black Church in Dublin, Ireland — a cathedral that’s been converted into an office space. The site listed a Los Angeles phone number that was busy every time 404 Media tried to call it. According to corporate paperwork filed in Ireland and reviewed by 404 Media, Media Nov Records was founded a little more than a year ago. Its listed address is the Black Church in Ireland but both of its shareholders gave addresses in Turkey.404 Media found four different YouTube pages managed by Media Nov Records. Each contained hundreds of videos — many with AI-generated art assets and music. The songs are sometimes cross posted between the different channels and are mostly looping electronic beats. Think low effort “lofi beats” knock offs. The art assets are footage of sports cars, anime girls, and AI-generated pictures of women. The songs are cross posted on multiple channels and often generate fewer than 100 views. Each also has few YouTube shorts that revolve around “random acts of kindness.” A Douyin (the Chinese version of TikTok) watermark is present in some of these videos.Media Nov Records told 404 Media that it operates 500 of these channels and “works with various artists, content creators, and music partners.” The company did not initially return emails or phone calls from Shokin or Loopmaster, but responded to an email from 404 Media.It said it would look into its copyright claim of Shokin’s track. “We remain willing to review the relevant ownership documentation, original audio files, and supporting evidence to investigate the copyright claim thoroughly. If an error is identified, we are committed to taking appropriate corrective action promptly,” it said.After 404 Media requested comment, Media Nov Records responded to Shokin and asked her to provide “relevant documentation supporting her ownership of the recording, including original audio files, recording evidence, original publication dates, and any other supporting materials,” which is a wild request considering that it has nothing to do with her recording and does not own the copyright.The company told 404 Media that Shokin and Loopmaster’s emails had gone to its spam folder. “Regarding ‘Bre Petrunko,’ we would like to clarify that the musical composition and arrangement rights associated with Philip Koutev’s work must be distinguished from the rights in any individual sound recording. Media Nov Records also holds certain rights relating to the relevant musical content,” the company told Shokin in an email reviewed by 404 Media.“Recording your own cover or performance does not automatically establish ownership of the underlying composition or arrangement. Likewise, rights in the underlying musical work do not automatically establish ownership of your particular recording,” Media Nov said. “It’s ironic that they’re in the copyright business,” Shokin said. “It’s not the arrangement that’s in question. It’s the voice and performance [...] they clearly have no clue what they’re talking about.”It's unclear why Media Nov Records brought Koutev into the conversation. 404 Media asked which song or work in its catalog triggered the copyright notice against Shokin but Media Nov Records did not respond. “That makes it really ridiculous,” Alfred Steiner, an artist and copyright lawyer, . “If it’s her voice and her playing instruments, what could she possibly be infringing if it’s a folk song from the 19th century?”The situation between Shokin and Media Nov Records sounded odd to Steiner. “I've seen lots of providers where you say ‘I have the rights’ and basically say nothing more than that, and they put it back because they’re taking a risk now. They’re harming her. If they just put it back, they’re at no risk,” he said. “It sounds, to me, like a small company — despite the fact that they represent or run 500 YouTube channels — that are understaffed and is using a lot of different tools, probably a lot of AI, to identify tracks that are ostensibly owned by its clients and then automatically filing takedown requests,” he said. “They’re probably taking down far more than they have the right to take down.”Minutes after it sent Shokin an email asking for proof she’d recorded the song, Media Nov Records followed up in an email addressed to both 404 Media and Shokin. “Following our review, Media Nov Records has decided to retract the copyright removal request for Samantha Shokin’s video. We are taking this step because the video has not generated revenue or received views, and we do not consider maintaining the removal request necessary at this stage,” it said. “However, this decision does not constitute a waiver of any rights we may hold. We intend to initiate appropriate legal proceedings regarding the underlying copyright dispute.”Around 24 hours later, Shokin’s original video was back up. A spokesperson for YouTube confirmed that it reinstated the video after the claimant withdrew their complaint. “It sounds like they got scared and feel like this is not a battle worth fighting,” Shokin said after seeing the email from Media Nov Records.“Submitting a takedown request for rights that you don’t have can subject you to liability which includes actual damages and costs and attorney’s fees,” Steiner told 404 Media. “Doing this on a slipshod, shotgun approach is inadvisable from my perspective. Of course, if all of the people you end up offending are small parties and don’t have the resources to respond through the court system, and you are a fly-by-night entity that is hard to pin down and nobody knows who you are [...] it can be difficult to get a remedy.”Shokin said she felt vindicated but was unhappy that it took a journalist emailing Media Nov Records to get them to listen to her. “They got my emails and they got Loopmaster’s email and they were just ignoring it because they only decided to respond because they got scared that it’ll be bad press,” she said. “It’s just not great all around. The whole system is broken. It feels like a broken system.”

item.title: The Kottke.org Video Closet
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Ok folks, I’m gonna apologize in advance for totally ruining any plans you might have had for the rest of your day. This weekend I knocked together the Video Closet, a simple tool for exploring & watching every YouTube & Vimeo video I’ve posted to KDO since 2014 that’s still live: almost 5400 of them in total. It’s like a YouTube that’s just for people who read KDO. Click a video to play it or click the title to go to the original post containing the video.The toughest thing about building the Video Closet was getting repeatedly distracted by videos while I was testing it. Seriously, don’t open this thing if you want to get any work done for the rest of the day!I also tweaked how video embeds work on the main site: there’s now a play button (plays the video in place), an “open on [service]” button (opens it in a new tab on YT or Vimeo), and, on desktop browsers, a widescreen button that embiggens the video in the current window and plays it (my favorite). I like rolling my own video embeds because the default ones from YT & Vimeo are heavy and include a lot of tracking — and now you can choose three different ways of watching, according to the customs of your people.

item.title: The 49ers Will Be The Best Team In Football If They Have To
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: First the San Francisco 49ers were too old to be the best team in football. Then they were too injured to be the best team in football. Now their defense against the lateral is too porous for them to be the best team in football. There's always something with them—the price they must pay for never having actually been the best team in football.Yet here we are, with them at 8-1 following a Jackson Pollock painting against the Dallas Cowboys, scoring 46 points but allowing 40 and coming within six laterals and two fumbles on the last play of the game from becoming a full-on clown show.The 49ers have been and still are the most baffling good team in the sport. They give off a pronounced vibe of being indomitable, and sometimes they actually are. Other times, like Sunday, they look like they have too much fun playing with their food. They fell behind 3-0, 10-7 and 16-10, then crushed Dallas for 20 consecutive minutes, and then went back to trading scores until the end of the game, which ended ludicrously enough with a Three Stooges skit that meant lots of work for 14 yards, and left a curious nation to wonder if they aren't just another pretty good team with just enough strengths to hide the flaws that will eventually undo them.

item.title: The Maple Leafs Are Still Finding New Lows
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: The Vancouver Canucks won their fourth hockey game of the 50-day-old NHL season Sunday night, but before you grab for your coat and panic-wave at the server to bring your check, this column will not be about the Vancouver Canucks. You deserve better than that. Hell, the Canucks deserve better than that.But not that much better, because this is about the Toronto Maple Leafs, who just wrapped up a historic 0-6-0 homestand.There is no city as devoted to its principal sports team than Toronto, based both on size of metropolitan area (7.1 million people) and monomaniacal allegiance (the Blue Jays, Raptors, Argonauts, Marlies, Sceptres, and Tempo are just things our northward friends notice until the lads' next morning skate), and there is no fan base as accustomed to or eager to resume its collective self-flagellation. They have entered their 60th year without either winning or appearing in a Stanley Cup Final, and the customers and their heralds are masters at not only the standard weariness of disappointment but performative fulmination. They love their team, a love which expresses itself as hatred because their team fails them as a function of their existence, and then they find out over time that they actually cut out the middlemen (the Leafs themselves) and end up falling in love with the hatred.

item.title: All About Burger King
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Burger King was born soon after McDonald's as a fast food burger outlet. It was first called Insta-Burger King, and they sold Insta-Burgers. That didn't last all that long, but what stayed was the idea of a flame-broiled burger being better than one that was fried. Still, Burger King tried, but could never overtake McDonald's as the number one burger outlet. They even fell to third for a time when Wendy's peaked. They always had the classic Whopper, but Burger King also became quite famous for their creepy king with a plastic face mascot and for the bizarre promotions they staged, some of which were so bad they disappeared before you ever heard of them. However, in the last few years, Burger King is trying some new ideas, the most intriguing being improvements to the food. Is it working? The comments are split, with half lauding delicious Burger King meals and the other half complaining about them. So... your mileage may vary.

item.title: The Bile High Club
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: Imagine being stuck on a grounded plane and suddenly remembering that the person in charge of Homeland Security is a guy named Markwayne. That was the experience for millions of travelers who faced a grounding of flights across America on Friday. And all those routes may have been brought down by a single router in Arkansas. (Gift Article): How Could a Router Lead to a Nationwide Ground Stop? “Aviation experts said it was likely that when the new router came online in Arkansas, the device began to send so much information that it overwhelmed the older equipment, which could not respond fast enough. That led to a cascade of issues.” The cascade of issues was followed by a cascade of blame deflection as Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy went on just about every Sunday morning talk show to refuse to apologize for the sky-emptying error, while Trump (surprise, surprise) blamed Biden. (By the time this is over, Trump and Duffy will be blaming the Wright Brothers.) At one point, Markwayne Mullin explained, “They were putting (in) new equipment and new technology. It was overwhelming the older system.” (That’s sort of how democracy felt after our entire leadership was replaced by characters from the movie, .) And when they say older technology, they’re not kidding. Here’s a headline from ten days ago: FAA to finally ditch floppy disks in what it calls ‘historic’ tech upgrade. How old is this tech? When pilots start up a 747, the system says, “You’ve got mail!” On some level, we have no idea whether this nightmare was caused by an Arkansas router, new technology overwhelming older technology, floppy disks flipping out, or something more nefarious, because the people providing us with the updates lie every time they speak. It’s enough to make you want to cancel your flights and just drive to your destination. Unfortunately, gas is too expensive for that.“Lemmy and Iggy, two carrion crows, are no strangers to a psychology lab. As study participants, they have helped scientists prove that birds can use tools to forage, learn numbers and count objects, and provided other insights into the ways birds think. Now, they’ve also revealed that birds can make staggeringly quick decisions, besting their human and nonhuman primate counterparts with ease.” (Gift Article): ‘Birdbrain’ Is a Misnomer. Crows Make Decisions Faster Than We Can. (And they don’t fall from the sky during software updates.) “A group of senior American officers, worried about exactly the type of attack that killed those six soldiers in Kuwait, told me they repeatedly urged commanders in the Middle East to deploy the new Ukrainian technology. The Pentagon ignored their warnings, which included detailed reports sent up the chain of command. Several of the officers who tried to raise the alarm about Iranian Shaheds have since been fired or forced into early retirement.” Simon Shuster in (Gift Article): The Pentagon Ignored a Warning About the Danger of Iran’s Drones.+ “Confirming a new GAO director as the GOP’s majority wanes would be a tremendous gift to President Donald Trump. Fights over federal spending will surely dominate the next two years and rushing through a pliant watchdog willing to turn a blind eye to Trump’s blatant seizure of funds would only further enable his illegality.” Trump getting his handpicked Government Accountability Office director confirmed would ensure that every spending bill Democrats pass is treated as a suggestion.+ Chopsticking the Landing: “Yesterday, for the first time ever, engineers successfully pulled off a —using the company’s Mechazilla tower’s ‘chopstick’ arms to snatch a starship the size of a skyscraper out of the sky after it had spent the past 22 hours in Earth’s orbit.” Not all air travel tech is outdated. (Gift Article): Awesome. (Some great video.)+ Carbon Emissions of Biggest U.S. Data Centers Already Rival Entire Countries. “The largest data centers in the United States are responsible for an estimated 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions annually — almost as much as entire countries like Bolivia or Denmark.” (Well, then, it’s pretty simple. We’re gonna have to get rid of Bolivia and Denmark.)+ His name is Pattinson. Robert Pattinson. And he’s the next James Bond. (I say no. My wife says yes. So it’s probably a good choice.)+ “Raye leads all nominees with a startling 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine. Tied for seven nominations each are Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers.” Grammy Nominations 2027.+ “One of the first casualties of a new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives is a St. Patrick’s Day parade in a beach town that has been celebrating its Irish American community for nearly 60 years.” (Oh, Florida, you should have gone blue.)+ Joe Rogan says Trump ‘lost most of the country‘ after the midterms. (Man who guided citizens over cliff now reports that the ground below is hard.)

item.title: The autobiography of Gunhild Lien Finseth
item.author: Minnesotastan
item.content:encoded: Since Mathilde has asked me to write down a little of my "pilgrimage" through life, I shall try in all frailty, though I suppose there will not be much coherence to it.I was born into this sinful world by parents Asle Eriksen Lien and wife Guri, née Jeglum, on January 23, 1847, and baptized on the 31st of the same year, in Torpo Annex, Hallingdal. On April 25, 1861, Father decided to take the children and travel to America due to unfortunate business affairs there. God led us with His fatherly hand over to the place where we landed. We set out from Drammen on May 6 and arrived in St. Peter on July 18, where we had an uncle whom we traveled to. They lived in a small log house, and there we climbed up on a ladder, fixed up a bed on the loft, and there we had plenty of visits from mosquitoes, so we had to make a "smudge" as they called it, took some scraps of wood chips and straw, set fire to it so the smoke chased the mosquitoes away from us somewhat; yes, such guesthouses they were in those days. Not a chair, only stools and benches and the like to sit on. The three oldest of us had to go out and get work, which was not very lucrative; my oldest sister Betsy worked for an American and got 50 cents a month, and I and my younger sister Guro got 25 cents a month. I must add that I did not get a cent in cash, but got a little calico for a dress and skirt, and Mother had to take a little wool for what I had earned.Yes, all that I did there at that time would have been a fair day's wage in the present time; yes, a maid would never have done all that I had to do. God had given me good health and strength to work both outside and inside. In September I was to get better wages with a family closer to St. Peter; they promised me 50 cents a month, and when it came down to it I got a pair of shoes and a "hood" for having worked there for 3 months. Milked the cows and worked outside.Then I traveled home for Christmas. In the month of March I was to go to town and try to get a place there, and it succeeded; got $4 a month there. My two sisters worked there as well. Mother and the three youngest lived out in the country about 11 miles north of St. Peter. Late in August or September [1862] the Indians broke out [the U.S.–Dakota War], so the country folk had to flee into town, leaving everything behind—both cattle, houses, and homes—and went to Sjabnee [Shakopee]. Good and well, the horses took a road southwestward; when they got as far as a mile away from our home, ours was spared from fire and destruction. My Mother decided to turn back to the little she had, and travel to Goodhue County.Two of our friends from Norway met us in Hastings with ox teams, took us and our things to Kittel Linnergaarden. There we stayed for a whole two years; that is to say, as a home to resort to. Those of us who were of use had to go out and work for a living. We came to Goodhue in late autumn 1861 [likely meant 1862]. I got work with Ole Nose for room and board when I set out and signed up for confirmation with Pastor Muus. We met either in a farmhouse or in a schoolhouse on the east side of Valley Grove. On the third Sunday in Advent I was confirmed in the house of John Hanson west of Valley Grove. That was for me a great and solemn day, and I must give Pastor Muus all the honor for it, because he explained it so clearly and thoroughly so that it would take root.Still, the promise was surely broken; I became far too lively and ungodly a youth, so I became just as ungodly as my companions. Yet I often felt remorse that I should behave so, with jesting and dancing, but my Catechism Explanation was always with me, and that was probably the only book I owned. Nor were there newspapers or magazines at that time.In the winter of 1863 we were supposed to go to English school. The schoolmaster was surely not very learned; I believe a schoolchild of the 4th grade would have come much further than our teacher. We had a couple of miles to walk and the snow became too deep to get through, so all I got of English school was about three weeks. Oh dear, how I have regretted that I did not get at least one winter term.Time and years passed; in the summer I was often at home and helped Mother to gather hay for her cows. In order to get someone to mow the hay, we had to help stack hay for them.In the spring of 1866 I was married to Ole K. Finseth on June 7th by Pastor Muus. We lived together with Anders Finseth until autumn, October 4th, when we moved into our new house, and there we lived together until the spring of 1912, on May 18th, when the Lord took my dear husband to Himself from the struggle to eternal joy and bliss.The Lord granted us 9 sweet children; the youngest the Lord took home to Himself at 5 years old in 1894. In the autumn of 1915 we traveled to Silverton, Oregon; the thought was to experience and find out whether the climate would be better than in Minnesota, and thought to live there 1 or 2 years, but the result became that I am here still.

item.title: Aphex Twin
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to Aphex Twin, a British electronic musician from Cornwall. The occasion is the release of the expanded edition of on the album’s 25th anniversary this past Friday. The album was originally released in 2001 after he accidentally left an MP3 player of unreleased tracks on a plane. He hadn’t intended to put out any of the music but the mistake forced his hand. The resulting album is a menagerie of prepared piano and acoustic compositions as well as jungle-esque frenetic tracks. contains his best-known song, “Avril 14th,” which now has many covers, several of which we featured in a mix this past April 14th. The new expanded edition includes five additional songs, three of which are alternative versions of “Avril 14th” and one of which is the legendary “Mangle 11.” For more, we highly recommend ’s recent Pitchfork featureWe wish you a great start to your week.
